verdict.reason:
Checked the working-tree plan file on disk (.agent/plans/delivery/design-system-completion.plan.md, lines 252-282 for W1, lines 540-547 for Cross-demo acceptance, plus W6.1 at 518-526 and the Decision log at 584-601). The claim's quotes are accurate: Cross-demo acceptance (line 540, applying to 'all four' demos) requires 'high-contrast and colour-safe reachable from the visible theme control — control present, keyboard-operable, ≤2 activations from page load — X18'. W1.2 (lines 268-278), the plain demo's authoring bullet, states only that the demo uses 'oak-theme.js for detection AND selection (kit-native — no React dependency; ... detection, selection, and persistence are already the kit runtime's contract)' plus a pre-paint head script. It does not state where in the page(s) the visible control lives, what element/component realizes it, or how it is authored into the 'export's three composed pages' markup.

I checked every plausible place the missing detail might actually live and confirmed the gap: (1) W6.1 'Cross-demo verification, mechanical' (line 518) only describes what to VERIFY post-hoc (attributes present before paint, persistence) — not the control's markup; (2) the Decision log (584-601) has no relevant row; (3) W0.3's Demos Charter (184-210) specifies the pre-paint script mechanism precisely but says nothing about the control widget; (4) I inspected the repo's actual studio-source export pages that W1.2 says the demo's markup will 'express the same compositions' of — of the three composed pages (Example Front Pages.html, Identity Switchboard.html, Identity White-Labelling.html), only Identity Switchboard.html contains any theme-selection markup, and it is a native `<select id="theme">` dropdown — a pattern squarely in the class the plan's own taste calibration (lines 88-92) records as REJECTED ('native form-control switchboards'), in tension with that same page being described there as CALLED GOOD for 'proper toggle-button controls'. That makes the omission more than cosmetic: the plan states a functional acceptance bar (X18) and a general taste constraint elsewhere, but never states the mechanism for the actual control's markup/component in the plain demo, and the one concrete precedent in-repo conflicts with the plan's own taste ruling. This is a real, verifiable specification gap in W1.2, matching the claim.

Also confirmed the plan generally holds itself to a 'mechanism declared/stated' discipline elsewhere (e.g. W0.3's exact per-demo pre-paint script placement, W2's schema/emitter mechanisms), so the absence of any stated mechanism for the control widget itself is a genuine departure from that discipline, not an inherent property of plan-level abstraction.

verdict.reason:
Core claim confirmed against the on-disk v2 plan (.agent/plans/delivery/design-system-completion.plan.md, working tree, modified per `git status`). Grepping the full 655-line file for "famil" turns up exactly five hits: line 397 ("W3.1 Curated adoption, sliced by component family"), 407-409 (W3.1's per-family test/acceptance language), 495 (unrelated — "amendment family"), and 578 (Sequencing's "each W3 family..."). Nowhere does the plan name what a family is, how many exist, or where one family's boundary ends and the next begins. It only defines a per-CLASS mapping rule in W3.0 (recipe class → component; modifier class → prop/variant union; layout primitive → composition component; utility → className passthrough) and a generated per-CLASS census in W0.1 ("component classes from `components.css`") — neither states a rule for grouping classes into families. I also checked the two authorities the plan leans on for this: ADR-213 §3 (docs/architecture/architectural-decisions/213-design-system-integration-and-component-architecture.md) gives only a "pointers, not specs" landing-sequence list of named candidate components (code chip/block, breadcrumbs, oak-band, masthead/footer) with no family taxonomy or count; PDR-132 (.agent/practice-core/decision-records/PDR-132-...md) governs review-round budgets only and never mentions families. So the concept is genuinely undefined everywhere it could plausibly live.

This matters practically: it leaves the W3.1 PR count/sequencing unestimable and the "coverage table rows for the family" acceptance line unverifiable against anything concrete, and it means the E47 disposition's claim of "applied" (dispositions.v2.md line 64: "W3.1 sliced by family") doesn't fully close the original v1 finding — E47's actual v1 text (findings.v1.json, expertFindings[47]) was about missing per-story describing-surfaces/cycle-decomposition ("state the describing surface... before the cycle decomposition is settled") and only suggested family-slicing as one example cure; naming the slicing axis without defining its values leaves the cycle decomposition still unsettled for W3.1 specifically.

One correction to the evidence offered: it says "W3.0 states 'Each family a single-story PR'; W3.1 repeats [it]" — that's inaccurate. I verified W3.0 (lines 387-396) contains no occurrence of "family" at all; the phrase "Each family a single-story PR" appears exactly once, in W3.1 (line 397), not twice across both stories. This doesn't undermine the underlying claim, which stands.

Severity: not blocking — a competent executor can infer a reasonable grouping (one family = one W3.0 recipe-class row plus its modifier/variant classes) from the mapping rule plus the generated census, and the plan's ultimate W3 done-ness bar (X27, "coverage table's mapping column complete against the census") is stated at the class level, which IS mechanically verifiable independent of family boundaries. So this is a real specificity/completeness gap worth curing (e.g., one added clause stating the family = grouping rule and either a count or a "derived mechanically from the W0.1 census + W3.0 mapping" pointer) but it doesn't structurally block W3 from starting or being verified at the class level. Rating "important" rather than "blocking."

verdict.reason:
Core textual observation confirmed, but the claim's evidence is partly misattributed and its practical severity is overstated.

Confirmed on disk (`.agent/plans/delivery/design-system-completion.plan.md`, working tree):
- W0.4 (lines 211-216) does say the census is "W2's input; explicit `depends_on` for W2 entry (X7)."
- W2's preamble (lines 283-296, "Direction settled per E4/E5/E67...") never names W0.4 or restates a dependency on it, nor does any W2.x story (checked W2.1-W2.10, lines 298-378) call back to W0.4 as a required input at its point of use — it cites the same underlying evidence id (E4) but not the workstream. So "not stated in W2's preamble" is literally true.

However, two problems with the claim as stated:

1. Evidence misattribution. E54/E69 (dispositions.v2.md lines 71, 86; adjudication.md line 22-24, "Live-plan collision") are about a completely different dependency: the cross-plan collision with the `design-system-integration` executing plan, where the plan-corpus validator refuses `depends_on` ids outside the anchored estate. They say nothing about W0.4/W2. The disposition that actually covers W0.4→W2 is **X7** ("W0.4 named as W2's input with explicit dependency," dispositions.v2.md line 137), which the claim does cite but then wrongly bundles with E54/E69's unrelated validator-limitation reasoning. Frontmatter `depends_on: []` (line 14) is a cross-plan-node field in this estate; W0.4→W2 is an intra-plan workstream edge that was never a frontmatter candidate regardless of the E54/E69 validator constraint — that constraint is irrelevant here.

2. Overstated consequence. The plan's single canonical sequencing statement — "## Sequencing and PR discipline" (line 578): "W0 → W1 → W2 → W3 → W4 → W5 → W6, with W1 gated only on W0" — already makes all of W0 (hence W0.4) a hard prerequisite for W1, and W1 a prerequisite for W2, transitively gating W2 on W0.4's completion. This is the plan's consistent convention: other coarse dependencies ("W1 gated only on W0," "each W3 family independent") are likewise stated once in this section and not repeated in each workstream's own preamble. A reader following the plan's stated execution order (or its document order, which lists all of W0 before W1 before W2) would complete W0.4 before ever reaching W2, so "a reader starting W2 work would not see they must wait" overstates the actual risk — it's a discoverability/cross-reference nit (W2 doesn't name its input inline), not an absent or hidden blocker.

Net: the defect is real but narrow — a missing inline cross-reference at W2's point of use, already covered at the coarse workstream-chain level and misdescribed by evidence that belongs to an unrelated finding (E54/E69).

verdict.reason:
Confirmed against the working-tree file as read from disk (lines 387-396 of .agent/plans/delivery/design-system-completion.plan.md). W3.0's acceptance line reads verbatim: "Acceptance (`repo-safe`: the amendments in the landing PR diff; the coverage table's mapping column complete against the census — X27)." No generator, script, or CI gate is named for the "complete against the census" clause — only a PR-diff read and a bare completeness assertion.

Traced X27 to its origin: droppedAtCap[27] in .agent/reports/design/plan-review-2026-08-02/findings.v1.json ("severity": "important", lens: testability), whose claim was "completeness is not explicitly tied to W0.1's census — a seat could create their own subset," with suggested_cure asking for a row schema (component name, export status, test URL, accessibility gate status) per W0.1 census class. dispositions.v2.md marks X27 "applied" at W3.0, but the actual v2 text only appended the words "against the census" — it did not add the row-schema or any named instrument the cure asked for.

This is a real, verifiable gap, and it contrasts sharply with sibling stories in the same file that DO name instruments for equivalent completeness claims: W0.1 ("census generator test... zero undispositioned rows") and W4.5 ("the gate fails when (a) a census entry has no demonstrating surface... the matrix gate in `pnpm check`"). W3.0 has neither. It also fails the plan's own Delivery contract in .agent/plans/plan-node-schema.md line 127-129, which defines `repo-safe` as requiring a cited instrument ("a test, validator, or CI check — cite the instrument") — W3.0's mapping-completeness clause is typed `repo-safe` but names none. This also shows the E79 disposition's claim ("Typed acceptance throughout") is not fully true for this specific clause: it carries the `repo-safe` tag but not the instrument the tag is supposed to guarantee.

Severity: the claim itself offered no severity label; I've set it to "important," matching the severity the original underlying finding (X27/droppedAtCap#27) was rated at, and consistent with the pattern of sibling "named instrument" findings in the same review. It is not "blocking" (this is a plan-authoring gap caught pre-execution, not a shipped defect), and it is not "minor" given the owner's explicit standing requirement that "every W0.1 census component class gets a recorded mapping decision" (line 385) — without a named mechanical check, that requirement is asserted rather than enforced.

expertFindings.section: W2 preamble + W2.5 + W4.4 (identity emitter / per-identity gate matrix / token-reference page)
expertFindings.claim: Oak is a configured identity for the runtime, asset and roster axes but is explicitly excluded from the token emitter, so the two stories that require a per-identity emitted token projection have no defined input for the primary identity — and W4.4 forbids the only surface that could serve it.
expertFindings.evidence: W2 preamble: "Oak's base kit keeps the ADR-213 §2 CSS→projection direction … never a second Oak token source", and W2.2 migrates each identity by replacing "the hand-authored sheet" — Oak has none (it IS `packages/design/oak-design-system/colors_and_type.css`). Yet W2.5 gates "over the identity's emitted token projection + pairings manifest" and W4.4 generates "from W2's per-identity emitted token projections (never the export's validator-only `dtcg/` during the dual-gate window)". Meanwhile W2.8 gives "each identity" a payload and W3.3 feeds the identity list from W2.1's schema, so Oak is in the configured set. Verified: no CSS→DTCG generator exists in-repo (`packages/design/oak-design-system/package.json` scripts are build/build:flat/sync:runtime/type-check/test/lint only); Oak's only projection is the studio-generated `dtcg/` set that W4.4 prohibits. Executed as written, W2.5 also removes the input from Oak's currently-landed four-theme contrast gate (`packages/design/oak-design-tokens/src/design-system-contrast.ts`).
expertFindings.suggested_cure: State the Oak asymmetry explicitly in the W2 preamble and give it a mechanism: either (a) Oak gets a manifest whose token block is a generated projection of the kit CSS (adding the CSS→DTCG generator as a named W2 story, which is what ADR-213 §2's "the `dtcg/` export is regenerated from it (CI checks the consistency)" already obligates), or (b) W2.5 and W4.4 declare a two-source rule — emitted projection for non-base identities, the kit's regenerated export for Oak — with the dual-gate-window exception stated for Oak's row rather than a blanket prohibition.

expertFindings.claim: The stated observable form — resolved theme and motion attributes present on the document element before first paint under each emulated OS signal — is falsified by the kit runtime's deliberate contract for two of the three signals, so all four demos fail the criterion or the kit gets wrongly changed.
expertFindings.evidence: `packages/design/oak-design-system/src/oak-theme.ts`: `apply()` does `delete el.dataset.theme` when there is no choice ("Explicit choices … SET the attribute so they beat a polarity-flipped brand default … no choice = no attribute"), `auto()` consults ONLY `(prefers-contrast: more)`, and `mapply()` does `delete el.dataset.motion` for `system` ("Motion has no choice(): 'system' IS its no-choice semantic (no attribute)"). Verified in the CSS: `colors_and_type.css` carries exactly one `prefers-color-scheme` query (line 586, filter-icon only) — dark polarity is delivered by `color-scheme` + `light-dark()`, never by an attribute. So under emulated `prefers-color-scheme: dark` or `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` with no stored choice, neither attribute is present by design.
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Re-state W6.1's observable form as the *resolved rendering* rather than attribute presence: assert the computed `color-scheme` / resolved role values (or the `data-motion` collapse via computed duration) before first paint, and reserve the attribute-presence cells for the stored-choice and `prefers-contrast: more` cases where the kit does set them. Name the no-attribute default as an asserted invariant so a future kit change that starts stamping attributes reddens.

expertFindings.section: W2.1 / W2.2 (identity manifest schema and emitter)
expertFindings.claim: The manifest is specified as referencing "a DTCG token file" (singular) for a roster of arbitrary themes, but DTCG 2025.10 defines no theme/mode mechanism and the kit composes roles with CSS `light-dark()`; the plan never reconciles the identity token shape with the estate's landed declared-base overlay model, and W2.5's contrast run over a sparse identity tree hits a failure mode ADR-213 warns about by name.
expertFindings.evidence: Live spec (designtokens.org/TR/2025.10/format/) confirms no modes/themes mechanism and no angle type. The kit's own export solves this with a per-theme file set — `dtcg/semantic.{light,dark,high-contrast,colour-safe}.json` — and its README records "The CSS composes these via `light-dark(a, b)`; the generator split each into `a` (light) and `b` (dark). 64 roles were split this way" (verified: 64 `light-dark(` occurrences in `colors_and_type.css`). ADR-213 §2 amendment 2026-07-19 makes this a declared-base overlay model with orphan detection (`validateThemeOverlayCoverage`) and states: "Contrast validation MUST compose base ⊕ overlay before resolution; validating a sparse overlay alone spuriously reports unresolved tokens." W2.5 says the matrix runs "over the identity's emitted token projection + pairings manifest (inheriting the base manifest by default)" with no composition step — the inherited 42-pair manifest addresses paths a sparse identity tree does not carry.
expertFindings.suggested_cure: In W2.1, specify the identity token block as a base tree plus one overlay tree per rostered theme (mirroring `semantic.<theme>.json`), with polarity pairs authored as light/dark arms the emitter composes into `light-dark()`, and require orphan detection via the landed `validateThemeOverlayCoverage`. In W2.5, add "base ⊕ overlay composed before resolution" to the stated mechanism and make an uncomposed-overlay run a red fixture.

expertFindings.claim: Seat-verdict (d) names the emitter's owning workspace but not the emitted CSS custom-property naming contract; the only flattener that workspace ships emits a namespace the kit does not read, so emitted brand CSS would be a silent no-op.
expertFindings.evidence: `packages/design/design-tokens-core/src/index.ts:46` — `toCssVariable(path)` returns `--oak-${path…join('-')}`, unconditionally Oak-prefixed and path-derived. ADR-213's 2026-07-20 exploration amendment confirms "Variable identity is derived from tree paths (`toCssVariable`), so any re-rooting renames every emitted CSS variable". But the kit's consumption surface reads bare role names: `components.css` contains 204 distinct `var(--…)` references and ZERO `var(--oak-…)` references (first-hand count). The white-label contract in `brand.css` likewise instructs overriding canonical bare roles and declares tier-1 `--oak-*` PRIVATE ("do not override them; they may change"). An emitter that flattens an identity tree through the landed path convention produces `--oak-semantic-text-primary`, which nothing in the kit reads.
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Add an explicit clause to W2.2: the emitter's output namespace is the kit's published role vocabulary (bare canonical role names for tier-2/3, `--oak-*` only for tier-1 primitives), with a mechanical check that every emitted custom property matches a role the kit's CSS actually reads, and that every kit role an identity must supply is emitted. Note in §Relationships that `design-tokens-core`'s existing `toCssVariable` convention is for the `oak-design-tokens` consumer only and is not reused here.

expertFindings.section: W2.4 + W2.1 (theme overlays parameterised over identity; colour-safe required by schema)
expertFindings.claim: Parameterising colour-safe over "identity-supplied palette slots" discards domain knowledge encoded in Oak's palette and leaves an accessibility-named theme with no mechanism that checks the property it is named for — the contrast gate cannot detect colour confusion.
expertFindings.evidence: `colors_and_type.css:690-704`: the colour-safe overlay re-points 13 roles onto a purpose-built colour-independent triad (`--oak-ci-blue`, `--oak-ci-vermilion-deep`, `--oak-ci-ochre`, plus tints) — an Ishihara-safe substitution, not a generic palette slot. W2.5's stated gate is token-pair contrast at AA/AAA thresholds, which is luminance-based and passes a red/green pair that is indistinguishable under deuteranopia. W2.1 requires "colour-safe defaults on", so every arbitrary identity ships a theme making that claim with nothing verifying it. The kit's own standing rule ("state is never colour alone", `components.css` header) lives in prose only.
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Add to W2.5 a colour-safety leg distinct from contrast: simulate deuteranope/protanope/tritanope transforms over the identity's success/error/warning/selected role set and assert a minimum perceptual separation between semantically-distinguishing pairs; where a mechanical check is refused, make colour-safe an owner-or-accessibility-expert sign-off gate recorded per identity rather than a schema default. Promote "state is never colour alone" into the W0.3 demos-tier DoD as a checked criterion.

expertFindings.section: W2.3 (theme roster generation) — the five hand-maintained lists
expertFindings.claim: Deriving `design-system-expectations.ts` from a generated roster would disarm the export-drift net that module exists to be; the story's own falsifier acceptance ("zero list edits") forces exactly that.
expertFindings.evidence: `packages/design/oak-design-tokens/src/design-system-expectations.ts` header: "THE single home for every number and name the gate pins against the imported export. Re-baseline this module at every studio sync; a mismatch is the gate telling you the export's shape drifted, not a number to bump silently." It pins `DESIGN_SYSTEM_THEMES`, owner-ratified `THEME_GATE_LEVELS` (HC=AAA, rest=AA, ratified 2026-07-20), `PALETTE_ROOTS`, per-theme `SEMANTIC_ROOTS`, `EXPECTED_MANIFEST_PAIR_COUNT = 42`, and the per-theme comparand count whose comment states "if it moves, a token changed class, not just value". W2.3 says the five lists "derive from it or are build-checked against it" and W2.6's theme-№N falsifier requires a config-minted theme to reach "`data-theme`, the matrix, and the labels with zero list edits".
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Split the roster consumers in W2.3: runtime union, React types and demo label maps DERIVE from the generated roster; `design-system-expectations.ts` is BUILD-CHECKED against it and stays hand-pinned (a new theme is a deliberate re-baseline, which is the gate working). Restate the theme-№N falsifier as "zero edits outside the pinned expectations module, and a required, reviewed re-baseline inside it".

expertFindings.claim: Requiring a per-theme binding for `forced-colors: active` encodes a wrong model of forced-colours mode and invites identities to declare a theme the user agent will override anyway.
expertFindings.evidence: W2.1 requires "per-theme OS-signal bindings (`prefers-color-scheme: dark`, `prefers-contrast: more`, `forced-colors: active`)". In forced-colours mode the UA substitutes system colours for author colours; the kit treats it accordingly as structural adaptation, not a theme — `components.css:1068-1080`: "Windows High Contrast Mode (forced-colors) — System colours win; shadows vanish. Real borders + transparent focus outlines … keep every state visible", emitting `border: … solid ButtonText`. `colors_and_type.css:597` states the same boundary explicitly: "Windows High Contrast Mode is handled separately via forced-colors in components.css; this theme is for users who choose it in-product."
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Restrict the schema's OS-signal binding axis to signals that actually select a theme (`prefers-color-scheme`, `prefers-contrast`), and model forced-colours as a separate required manifest obligation: the identity's declared CSS layer must carry a forced-colours adaptation block, gate-proven by the W2.5 matrix's forced-colours render cell, with no theme name attached.

expertFindings.section: W0.2(c) (the `prefers-contrast` route) — the two new gate cells
expertFindings.claim: The named acceptance cells are one-sided: neither tests that an explicit non-HC choice survives an OS contrast request, and the landed theme architecture makes the obvious implementation break exactly that case.
expertFindings.evidence: W0.2(c) requires "a `@media (prefers-contrast: more)` CSS mapping onto the high-contrast block scoped so an explicit non-system choice wins" and names two cells — stored-`system` + `emulateMedia contrast:more` → applied; `javaScriptEnabled:false` + contrast more → applied. Both are positive. Verified in `colors_and_type.css:558-566`: `[data-theme='light']` and `:root[data-theme='light']` declare ONLY `color-scheme: light` — the light theme re-declares none of the ~73 semantic roles. A media block declaring the HC role set at `:root` (0,1,0) therefore beats the base `:root` block on source order and is not beaten by an explicit light/dark/colour-safe attribute, silently forcing high-contrast on users who chose otherwise.
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Name the scoping mechanism in the story (`@media (prefers-contrast: more) { :root:not([data-theme]) { … } }` is the shape the kit's "explicit choice always sets the attribute" contract supports) and add the negative cell to acceptance: stored explicit `light` (and `dark`, and `colour-safe`) + `emulateMedia contrast:more` → high-contrast NOT applied, JS enabled and disabled.

expertFindings.claim: Identity DATA has no declared workspace home or delivery path to the four demos, so W2.6's thinness boundary rules have no endpoints to bind and the ADR-041 obligation map omits the row the emitter's landing needs; the ADR-213 §1 move-out that W2.2 fires is unstated.
expertFindings.evidence: W2 names `design-tokens-core` as owning "schema + validators + emitter" (the mechanism) but no workspace for identity manifests, token files, assets or emitted CSS. W2.6(c) requires depcruise/ESLint rules "no framework module imports identity data; no identity data imports framework source" — undeclarable without a data home. §Relationships lists ADR-041 amendments only for the W1.1/W5.1 demo rows. Verified that the sheets W2.2 replaces are already product-consumed: `demos/oak-design-showcase/tools/kit-asset-parity.ts` maps `studio-source/whitelabel/freedonia/brand-full.css` → `public/brands/freedonia/brand.css` (and the same for creature), served by `components/useIdentity.ts` at `/brands/${identity}/brand.css`. ADR-213 §1: "A studio-source file that becomes consumed by product code moves out and under the full gate in the same change." W1.2 declares §1 not-triggered for pages; nothing states it for identity sheets, where it does bite.
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Add a W2 story creating the identity-data home (a workspace or a gated non-`studio-source` directory) with its dated ADR-041 row and its dependency-direction edges, add that row to §Relationships' ADR-obligations map, and state in W2.2 that the freedonia/creature migrations execute the ADR-213 §1 move-out, retiring or re-pointing the `KIT_ASSET_COPIES` parity rows in the same change.

expertFindings.section: W4.4 (the token-reference page) — the computed-style parity test
expertFindings.claim: "One computed-style PARITY test" cannot hold: the generated value and the rendered cascade differ by construction for the composed and expression-valued token classes, and parity is a per-identity × per-theme property.
expertFindings.evidence: First-hand counts: 64 `light-dark(` compositions in `colors_and_type.css` (generated value is an expression, computed value is one resolved arm depending on `color-scheme`); 3 `color-mix()`/`calc()` declarations in `colors_and_type.css` and 14 in `components.css`. The kit's own `dtcg/README.md` records "15 tokens carry `color-mix()`/`calc()` expressions … verbatim in `$value` — DTCG has no function syntax", and ADR-213 declares `runtime-computed` a value class "excluded from static contrast resolution by contract". W4.4 states "never runtime `getComputedStyle` as the value source — one computed-style PARITY test proves generated values match the rendered cascade".
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Re-scope the parity acceptance in W4.4: parity runs per identity × theme over the statically-resolvable class only (six-digit hex comparands and unitful scalars, reusing the landed `toHexComparand` filter), with `runtime-computed` and composed-shorthand tokens carrying an explicit recorded disposition (rendered specimen, no value assertion). State the cell count so a silently shrinking parity check is visible, matching W2.5's pinned-cell-count discipline.

expertFindings.claim: The token-reference page must discriminate presentation by token type, but a large fraction of the landed token corpus carries no `$type` and the plan schedules no cure — the disposition ledger's claim that v2 removes all `$type` guessing is not backed by a story.
expertFindings.evidence: Live DTCG 2025.10: `$type` must be resolvable from the token or its closest parent group, and tools "MUST NOT attempt to guess the type". First-hand count over `packages/design/oak-design-system/dtcg/`: `component.json` 6 typed / 68 untyped; `semantic.light.json` 92 typed / 54 untyped; `semantic.high-contrast.json` 65/6; `semantic.dark.json` 61/3; `primitives.json` 93/5. The export's own README states "`$type` is heuristic … composite values (shadows, font shorthands) omit it", and `design-system-expectations.ts` calls its pinned comparand count "the drift net for the export's heuristic `$type`". `dispositions.v2.md` E0 asserts "no `$type` guessing anywhere" and routes export `$type` completeness to W0.5 as a "sync-back candidate" — i.e. to an owner-driven, unenumerated intake, not a story.
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Make `$type` completeness a named gap-census row in W0.1(b) with an implementing story: add group-level `$type` declarations (the spec's inheritance mechanism covers most of the untyped composites cheaply) and a completeness check that fails on any leaf whose type is unresolvable. Make W4.4's root-coverage check a type-coverage check too, so an untyped token cannot reach the reference page as an undifferentiated string.

expertFindings.claim: "Tokens under `semantic.` / `component.` per the tier detector" contradicts the landed root convention: the kit's trees are kit-native-rooted, and the named tier detector classifies those roots as palette.
expertFindings.evidence: `packages/design/design-tokens-core/src/index.ts:25-36` — `getTokenTier` returns `semantic` only for a `semantic` root segment, `component` for `component`, and `palette` for everything else. The kit's actual semantic trees root at `bg`, `border`, `color`, `control`, `ease`, `filter`, `focus`, `motion`, `scrim`, `shadow`, `state`, `surface`, `text`, `type` — pinned as `SEMANTIC_ROOTS` in `design-system-expectations.ts` and validated by `validateTreeRoots`. ADR-213's 2026-07-20 exploration amendment replaced the fixed `color.`/`semantic.`/`component.` root requirement with per-consumer allow-lists precisely because "the export ships kit-native trees".
expertFindings.suggested_cure: State the off-horizontal tokens' root in the kit-native vocabulary the identity trees actually use (e.g. a `tilt` or `transform` root added to the identity allow-list) rather than citing `semantic.`/`component.`, or state that identity token files use the normalised `semantic.`/`component.` convention and name the mapping to the kit vocabulary that the emitter applies — currently the plan implies one convention where two exist.

expertFindings.claim: The kit's own CSS already renders off-horizontal geometry, so a degrees-token dimension lands with an unstated exemption inside the package the framework generalises from, and the owner's "Oak has none" is unverifiable as stated.
expertFindings.evidence: `packages/design/oak-design-system/components.css` carries 7 hardcoded rotations (lines 637, 685, 842, 847, 899, 903, 908 — `rotate(45deg)`, `rotate(225deg)`, `rotate(-45deg)`, `translateY(-70%) rotate(45deg)`), glyph constructions for arrows/marks. The literal instrument the plan re-homes in W0.8 does flag angle units — `deg`, `rad`, `grad`, `turn` are in the `UNITS` set of `demos/oak-design-showcase/tools/css-literal-values.ts` — but its roster is demos-only, so the kit's own instances are unscanned in both the current and the re-homed shape.
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Add one sentence to W2.7 drawing the boundary: glyph-construction rotation (borders forming a chevron/tick) is out of the identity off-horizontal dimension and stays literal or gets its own named convention; identity tilt on content blocks is tokenised. Record the 7 kit instances as a dispositioned row in W0.1(b)'s gap census so the exemption is stated, not silent.

expertFindings.claim: The plan exposes `applied()` as a `useSyncExternalStore` snapshot but enumerates the kit's notification points exhaustively as "every `set`/`motion.set` plus a `storage`-event bridge" — which omits the only route that actually changes the applied theme without a `set()`. Executing as written yields an `applied()` snapshot that is permanently stale after an OS contrast change, and W3.2's own acceptance line ("store unit tests incl. the cross-writer staleness case") does not touch it.
expertFindings.evidence: `packages/design/oak-design-system/src/oak-theme.ts:82-94` — `auto()` reads `matchMedia('(prefers-contrast: more)')`; `:117` `apply(stored() || auto() || null)`; `:121-130` a live `change` listener calls `apply(auto() || null)` with no `set()` involved. W0.2(c) widens this route further (stored-`system` consults `auto()`). react.dev/reference/react/useSyncExternalStore: subscribe must "listen for the browser's change events", and React only re-reads a snapshot when subscribe fires. W6.1/W0.2(c) cells assert the DOM attribute under `emulateMedia` set before load, never a runtime media flip observed through the React snapshot. Additionally, `OakThemeStore` (`packages/design/oak-design-react/src/oak-theme-store.ts:67-76`) has ONE `getServerSnapshot(): undefined` shared by all selectors, so "getServerSnapshot returning the neutral value" has no place to live without an API change.
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Re-state the kit contract as "listeners fire from `apply()` (the single application point), not from `set()`", so the automatic contrast route, the W0.2(c) `system` route, and any future auto route notify by construction. Name the store shape explicitly (`getApplied()` + `getAppliedServerSnapshot()`, or a selector-keyed snapshot API) and state what "neutral" is (`'light'` vs `undefined`) and what the control renders in that state. Add an acceptance cell: no stored choice, toggle `emulateMedia({ contrast: 'more' })` AFTER load, assert the React `applied()` snapshot moves.

expertFindings.section: W3.0 / W3.4 — landing-sequence obligations and server/client boundary policy
expertFindings.claim: W3.4's policy ("presentational tier components ship without `'use client'`; only interactive residents carry it") is unimplementable against `oak-design-react`'s current build and export shape, and no story in the plan changes that shape. Executed as written, every `'use client'` directive is silently discarded at build and the whole tier collapses into one module with no client boundary.
expertFindings.evidence: `packages/design/oak-design-react/package.json` — single `"."` export → `./dist/index.js`. `tsup.config.ts` → `createLibConfig()` → `tsup.config.base.ts` `SHARED_DEFAULTS` = `bundle: true, splitting: false`, entry `['src/index.ts']`. Empirically verified with the exact toolchain this repo resolves (tsup@8.5.1 → esbuild 0.28.1, symlink confirmed): bundling `src/index.ts` re-exporting a module whose first line is `'use client';` produced `dist/index.js` with the directive absent and no warning. react.dev/reference/rsc/use-client: the directive "must be at the very beginning of a file" and marks "the module and its transitive dependencies as client code" — a single bundled module cannot host a mixed boundary. Separately, the package lists every dep under `devDependencies`; tsup externalises `dependencies`/`peerDependencies` only (`tsup/dist/chunk-VGC3FXLU.js:81,90`), so adding `react` as a devDependency would inline React into `dist` → duplicate React → "Invalid hook call" across two demo consumers. `packages/design/oak-design-ink/package.json:32-35` already sets the estate convention (`peerDependencies: { react }` + devDependency mirror).
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Add a W3.0 packaging story ahead of W3.1: per-component entries with subpath `exports` (or `splitting: true`/preserve-modules), a directive-preserving esbuild plugin or banner, `external: ['react','react-dom','react/jsx-runtime']`, `react` (and `react-dom` where needed) as `peerDependencies` with devDependency mirrors, `jsx: 'react-jsx'` in `tsconfig.build.json`, and make W3.4's "module-level assertion test over the tier's exports" assert on `dist/*` — the built artefact is where the directive is lost, not `src/*`.

expertFindings.section: W4.6 — Tailwind discipline in the showcase (seat-verdict (a))
expertFindings.claim: Seat-verdict (a) — "tier components paint via KIT CLASSES; Tailwind's role-mapped utilities are the showcase's page/layout COMPOSITION vocabulary" — rests on a cascade assumption that is false in this repo. Kit CSS is entirely unlayered; Tailwind v4 emits all utilities inside `@layer utilities`. Unlayered normal declarations always beat layered ones, so any composition utility touching a property a kit recipe already sets is a silent no-op. W3.1's "`className` accepted and merged after kit classes" compounds the error: class order in the attribute has no cascade meaning at all.
expertFindings.evidence: `node_modules/.pnpm/tailwindcss@4.3.3/.../index.css` line 1: `@layer theme, base, components, utilities;` and tail: `@layer utilities { @tailwind utilities; }`. `grep -rn "@layer" packages/design/oak-design-system/*.css` → zero hits (verified: styles.css, colors_and_type.css, components.css, oak-icons.css, print.css). MDN `@layer`: "Styles that are not defined in a layer always override styles declared in named and anonymous layers" and "all normal declarations within CSS layers have a lower priority than declarations declared outside of a layer". `components.css` sets padding/gap/radius/colour/font/border on the recipes the tier will paint with (e.g. `.oak-btn` at :294-356). W4.6's exit check only detects the forbidden direction (recipe re-expressed as utilities); it is structurally blind to a permitted composition utility losing.
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Settle layering in W0.3/W4.6 as an explicit decision, not an implicit assumption. Either (a) state and lint the invariant that composition utilities apply only to elements carrying NO kit recipe class (wrappers), which also makes the exit check mechanical; or (b) import kit CSS into a named cascade layer at each demo entry (`@import '…/styles.css' layer(oak-kit);`) with the layer order declared relative to Tailwind's. Add a mechanical cell that plants a composition utility on a kit-classed element and asserts the computed value, so the failure mode is visible rather than silent.

expertFindings.claim: The plan's stated ground for seat-verdict (b) is wrong: "`styled(Component)` works because of W3.1's className-merge contract". className merge makes the styled class PRESENT; it does not make it WIN. styled-components v6 emits single-class rules at the same specificity as `.oak-btn`, both unlayered, so the winner is head source order — which differs between Next dev and prod and is further out-ranked by the demo's brand sheet convention.
expertFindings.evidence: Same cascade facts as the W4.6 finding (kit CSS unlayered; MDN layer precedence). styled-components v6 generates single-class selectors, specificity (0,1,0), identical to `.oak-btn`. Under the App Router registry, styled rules reach the head via `useServerInsertedHTML` while `app/globals.css` (which `@import`s the kit — `demos/oak-design-showcase/app/globals.css:13`) is emitted as a separate head asset; relative order is not fixed by the plan. `demos/oak-design-showcase/components/useIdentity.ts` docblock records the estate already relying on head order for exactly this reason: the brand link is "appended at the END of `document.head`, so the brand sheet loads after every bundled sheet and wins the cascade at equal specificity".
expertFindings.suggested_cure: W5.2 must state the override mechanism, not assert an outcome: either the tier's kit CSS is layered (so unlayered styled rules win deterministically), or styled components use the `&&` specificity bump / a declared `StyleSheetManager` layer. Add an acceptance cell asserting a `styled(TierButton)` background/padding override actually computes in both `next dev` and `next build && next start`.

expertFindings.section: W3.2 — Theme runtime completion (the storage-event bridge)
expertFindings.claim: A `storage`-event bridge that only re-emits to React listeners cannot cure the staleness W3.2 names, because the kit runtime caches the choice in a module-local variable that a cross-context write never touches. React would re-read an unchanged snapshot, `Object.is` would match, and no re-render would occur — while the DOM attribute also stays stale.
expertFindings.evidence: `packages/design/oak-design-system/src/oak-theme.ts:61` `let current: OakThemeName | null = null`; `:95-97` `get()` returns `current || stored() || auto() || 'light'`; `:102-104` `choice()` returns `current || stored()`. Once this context has called `set()` once, `current` is non-null and both accessors return the stale in-memory value indefinitely regardless of what another tab wrote. Same shape for `mcurrent` at `:145`/`:154-167`.
expertFindings.suggested_cure: State the bridge's obligation in the story: on a `storage` event for `oak-theme`/`oak-motion`, the kit must reset `current`/`mcurrent` from the incoming value (null on removal), call `apply()`, THEN emit. Acceptance cell: two browser contexts sharing origin — write in A, assert B's `data-theme` attribute AND `choice()` both move. If cross-context sync is not actually wanted, drop the bridge and reword the story's purpose clause, which currently promises it.

expertFindings.section: W3.0 / W3 preamble — the class→construct mapping rule
expertFindings.claim: W3.0's mapping rule is unconditional ("recipe class → component"), and W3's preamble makes coverage = a recorded mapping decision for every census component class. Composed, those two mandate a component per kit recipe — which is exactly the systematic class-library wrap ADR-213 §3 rejects, and is at odds with §3's "curated adoption" framing with four named seed candidates. Disposition E14's claim that "no re-wrap mandate remains, so the §3 rejection stands unamended" is not supported by the plan text.
expertFindings.evidence: `packages/design/oak-design-system/components.css` carries 65 base `.oak-*` recipe/layout classes (107 including modifiers and elements) — verified by enumeration: `.oak-accordion .oak-band .oak-banner .oak-block … .oak-worked-example`. ADR-213 §3 Standing rules: "Re-wrapping the class library in a framework component layer remains rejected (it would fork the tier-3 contract). This question is settled here and is not re-litigated per widget." §3 amendment 2026-07-23: "a curated, owned React component tier … first candidates: code chip/block surface, breadcrumbs, `oak-band` tone modifiers, masthead/footer site chrome".
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Make `class-only (no component; demonstrated in the showcase via `className`)` an explicit, first-class mapping outcome alongside the other three, and state the curation criterion that decides recipe→component (interaction model, prop variance, repeated composition across pages). If systematic mapping IS the intent, carry a dated ADR-213 §3 amendment in W3.0's landing-sequence set rather than asserting the standing rejection is untouched.

expertFindings.section: W3.1 — Curated adoption, sliced by component family
expertFindings.claim: W3.1 specifies hand-rolled interaction models for every interactive component, but ADR-213 §3's decision table routes new hard widgets to Base UI headless primitives and explicitly grades hand-rolled widgets as "candidate evidence, not gate-passing evidence". The plan never mentions Base UI, never states a construction-path decision, and never carries §3's app-shell prerequisites — yet the census will hand it modal, accordion, disclosure and choice widgets.
expertFindings.evidence: Kit recipes include `.oak-modal`, `.oak-accordion`, `.oak-disclosure`, `.oak-quiz`, `.oak-choice`, `.oak-select` (enumerated from `components.css`). ADR-213 §3 table: "New hard widget (React app) → Base UI headless primitives, styled by the same classes/tokens — adopted at first materialised need (a ticket, never an anticipation), pinned exact"; standing rules: "Existing hand-rolled APG widgets are grandfathered … Grandfathered code is candidate evidence, not gate-passing evidence". §3 also names app-shell prerequisites for Base UI: "`isolation: isolate` on the app root container (portal stacking) and `position: relative` on `body` (iOS 26+)". `grep -ci "Base UI"` on the plan → 0.
expertFindings.suggested_cure: W3.1 states the construction-path decision per interactive family: Base UI (pinned exact) as the default per §3, hand-roll only with a recorded ground; the wrapped-widget checklist runs either way. Carry §3's app-shell prerequisites into the W1.1/W5.1 workspace contracts and the W4 showcase acceptance, since portal-based widgets fail silently without them.

expertFindings.claim: W3.3 makes identity React-owned ("a layout-level provider") while theme is runtime-owned (kit trunk + React adapter), and simultaneously requires "a pre-paint identity bootstrap beside `oak-theme.js`" — two writers of one axis, in two workspaces, with the story sitting in the React-tier workstream. The non-trivial mechanism (load-then-swap, generation counter, preload) then lives in React and is unavailable to the plain and styled demos, contradicting the standing owner requirement that identities be trivially arbitrary and the system apply to plain HTML and CSS.
expertFindings.evidence: `demos/oak-design-showcase/components/useIdentity.ts` already carries the whole mechanism in React and documents the gap the plan is trying to close: "Identity deliberately does NOT persist across reloads: persistence would need a second pre-paint bootstrap to avoid a flash of Oak brand (the exact problem oak-theme.js solves for themes)." The load-then-swap rationale ("an in-place href update drops the outgoing sheet a frame before the incoming one joins the cascade") and the generation counter are ~90 lines of React-side logic that a plain-HTML demo cannot consume. The plan's §Out-of-scope records identity switching in plain/styled as a reversible assumption (X14), so the React-only shape prices that reversal at a full re-implementation.
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Mirror the theme trunk: an `oakIdentity` kit runtime (`get`/`choice`/`set`/`subscribe`, pre-paint application, load-then-swap, persistence) owned by the same workspace as `oak-theme.js`, and reduce W3.3 to a `useSyncExternalStore` adapter plus a children-slot provider. State the owning workspace explicitly — W3.3 currently straddles the kit and the React tier without naming either.

expertFindings.claim: The styled demo is given two painting mechanisms with no declared boundary: W5.2 consumes tier components that paint via kit classes, W5.3 requires "every styled component reads roles through `var()`". Nothing states which surfaces each owns. The two collide in the cascade (see the seat-verdict (b) finding), and if the tier paints most of the page the demo renders visually identical to the showcase — failing both its own purpose (demonstrating the styled-components consumption path) and the owner's "each and every demo … wow" bar.
expertFindings.evidence: W5.2: "the styled demo CONSUMES `oak-design-react` … `styled(Component)` works because of W3.1's className-merge contract". W5.3: "every styled component reads roles through `var()`". W3.1: tier components "consume kit classes (`.oak-btn`, `.oak-tag`, …) with variants as props". No story assigns surfaces to mechanisms. The §Quality bar applies the wow checkpoint per demo (W5.4).
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Declare the split in W5.1/W5.2: tier components for kit-covered recipes; styled-components for demo-local page composition, layout and chrome the kit does not cover. Add an explicit differentiation line to W5.4 (what makes this demo visually its own thing) so the wow checkpoint has something to judge beyond a re-render of the showcase.

expertFindings.section: W3.2 / W3.0 — the tier's contract-only kit edge
expertFindings.claim: W3.2 changes the `OakThemeRuntime` shape (adding `subscribe`, and an `applied` accessor), but that interface is re-declared by hand in two places across a contract-only edge with no parity mechanism, and the plan does not state whether the new members are optional for a runtime that failed to load — a state the store's existing design treats as first-class.
expertFindings.evidence: `packages/design/oak-design-react/src/oak-theme-store.ts:48-57` re-declares `OakThemeRuntime` "verbatim from `oak-design-system/src/oak-theme.ts` (contract-only edge — the kit ships no type declarations)"; the kit's copy is at `packages/design/oak-design-system/src/oak-theme.ts:34-40`. The store's two-level `undefined`/`''` gate exists because the runtime can be absent — `demos/oak-design-showcase/components/Switchboard.tsx` docblock: "coupling its availability to an unrelated subsystem's liveness would remove the page's headline interaction if the pre-paint script were ever blocked (e.g. a strict CSP)".
expertFindings.suggested_cure: W3.2 acceptance gains a contract-parity assertion between the kit interface and the tier's re-declaration (or the kit ships the `.d.ts` and the tier imports it), and the story states `subscribe` optionality plus the store's behaviour when the runtime is absent (no-op unsubscribe returned, snapshots still readable through the existing gate).

expertFindings.section: W4.6 — Tailwind discipline in the showcase
expertFindings.claim: "W4 exit check asserts no kit recipe re-expressed as utilities" is stated as a judgement with no mechanism, unlike every other gate in the plan. As written it will be discharged by assertion at exit, which is the failure mode the plan elsewhere works hard to eliminate.
expertFindings.evidence: W4.6 pairs a genuinely mechanical check ("the arbitrary-value ESLint check (`-\[` pattern in JSX class strings, plus role-name resolution for colour/spacing utilities)") with the exit check, which has no stated implementation, no red-proof, and no named test — while the plan's own §First-principles check and §Quality bar insist gates are mechanical and W2.6 requires each falsifier be "proven biting by mutation once".
expertFindings.suggested_cure: State the check as the lintable inverse: an element bearing a kit recipe class carries no painting-category utility (bg/text/border/radius/shadow/padding/font); elements without a kit class may carry composition utilities only. That reuses the JSX class-string visitor W4.6 already builds, red-proves on a planted violation, and doubles as the cure for the silent-loss problem in the cascade-layer finding.

expertFindings.claim: The prop contract's "semantic element choice explicit (`as`/`Link` variant)" is either a Next.js coupling inside a React-binding package or an unspecified API. Neither is safe to leave to implementation: a `Link` variant that imports `next/link` breaks the binding grammar ADR-213 §3 establishes, and an open polymorphic `as` lets a consumer render a `<div>` where the accessibility contract requires `<button>`/`<a>`.
expertFindings.evidence: ADR-213 §3 amendment: "The owned components live in a new React binding package … React is the first binding with materialised need; any later binding (Astro, Nuxt, vanilla helpers) takes the same downstream-sibling shape" — the tier is the React binding, not the Next binding. `packages/design/oak-design-react/package.json` has no `next` dependency and correctly should not. Three of four demos are Next apps, so the pressure to reach for `next/link` is real.
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Choose and state one: a render/`asChild` slot prop (the consumer passes its own `<Link>`), with the rendered element union constrained to `button | a` so the semantic contract cannot be broken by a prop. Record it in W3.1's contract line alongside `className` and ref-as-prop.

expertFindings.claim: Fixtures-as-parity changes what it proves under W3.1's class-consumption rewrite, and W3.0 re-homes it from `ws-fixtures-parity` without saying so. The migration will otherwise be scored against a claim it no longer makes.
expertFindings.evidence: ADR-213 §3 established fixtures-as-parity because the compiled React components were an INDEPENDENT implementation consuming the same tier-3 tokens — verified in `packages/design/oak-design-system/studio-source/components/OakButton/OakButton.jsx`, which paints entirely through an inline `style` object reading `--btn-*`/`--bg-btn-*` tokens, never through `.oak-btn`. Once the tier paints via kit classes (W3.1), markup drift is impossible by construction; the fixture then proves only that each prop combination selects the right class string.
expertFindings.suggested_cure: State the new claim in W3.0: the fixture is a class-selection contract per prop combination, not a drift check between two independent implementations. That also lets W3.1's per-family RED ("the family's first fixture") be written against something falsifiable.

expertFindings.claim: W3.1 correctly deletes the seed's `style` prop, but combined with unlayered kit classes the surviving `className` escape hatch cannot override a kit recipe at equal specificity. The tier would ship with no supported call-site variation route, which in practice produces `!important` or a fork.
expertFindings.evidence: `studio-source/components/OakButton/OakButton.jsx` accepts and spreads a `style` prop as the consumer override. W3.1: "no `style` prop" and "`className` accepted and merged after kit classes". Kit CSS is unlayered (`grep -rn "@layer" packages/design/oak-design-system/*.css` → zero hits), so a consumer class ties `.oak-btn` on specificity and is decided by stylesheet order the consumer does not control.
expertFindings.suggested_cure: State the sanctioned variation route in the prop contract: add a kit modifier class, or forward a declared set of CSS custom-property hooks the component sets on its root. Pair it with the layering decision so the route actually wins.

expertFindings.claim: The charter rule "a variant whose DOM order and visual order diverge is a defect to re-author, not a feature", mechanised in W4.2 as a Tab-walk asserting `getBoundingClientRect` monotonicity, contradicts the owner's standing requirement that CSS re-order page elements non-trivially, contradicts the estate's own governance on the subject, and would gate-fail exactly the compositions the strategic parent exists to prove.
expertFindings.evidence: <repo>/docs/governance/one-html-many-css-compositions.md §15 (line 796): "For the present objective, this does **not** mean visual restructuring is illegitimate. It means the canonical HTML should represent a defensible base narrative, while themes should be tested to ensure visual movement does not create a confusing focus path." §6 (lines 334-405) and §15 document `order` and Grid placement as the intended re-composition tools, and lines 811-836 name `reading-flow`/`reading-order` as the mechanism, to be used as progressive enhancement. Live check of MDN `reading-flow`: Limited Availability / experimental, not Baseline — so on today's browsers DOM order still drives speech and sequential-navigation order. A single fixed DOM serving three identities' composition maps cannot be visually monotonic in all three, so the W4.2 gate fails every genuinely re-ordered variant. Separately, 2D visual order is not a total order: `getBoundingClientRect` monotonicity has no correct definition for a legitimate multi-column layout.
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Replace the charter rule with the governance doc's actual rule: the canonical DOM carries a defensible base narrative (SC 1.3.2 Meaningful Sequence when linearised), and each composition variant DECLARES its intended reading sequence in the page-set artefact. Mechanise as: (a) a linearisation check on the base DOM; (b) the Tab-walk asserts the variant's DECLARED sequence, not raw geometry; (c) `@supports (reading-flow: …)` progressive enhancement per variant, with the non-supporting path proven acceptable by the declared-sequence check; (d) SC 2.4.3 judged against the declared sequence. Keep 'defect to re-author' only for variants that cannot state a coherent sequence.

expertFindings.section: W2.1 (identity manifest schema, per-theme OS-signal bindings) + W0.2(c)
expertFindings.claim: The schema models contrast level and colour-vision safety as members of one flat theme roster and binds each OS signal to a single theme, with no rule for composing signals. Because the kit's high-contrast and colour-safe themes hard-set `color-scheme: light`, this structurally forces every dark-preferring user who requests more contrast (or needs the colour-safe palette) onto a white canvas — now replicated per identity by schema mandate.
expertFindings.evidence: packages/design/oak-design-system/colors_and_type.css:598-600 `[data-theme='high-contrast'] { color-scheme: light; --bg-primary: var(--oak-white) … }` and :690-692 `[data-theme='colour-safe'] { color-scheme: light; … }`. packages/design/oak-design-system/src/oak-theme.ts:82-94 `auto()` returns `'high-contrast'` on `prefers-contrast: more` with no consultation of `prefers-color-scheme`; :117 applies it pre-paint. packages/design/oak-design-tokens/src/design-system-expectations.ts:15 pins the roster at four themes — there is no dark high-contrast and no dark colour-safe anywhere in the corpus. The signals are independent (dark × more-contrast × forced-colors × reduced-motion); motion is already correctly modelled as an orthogonal axis (`data-motion`, colors_and_type.css:496-521) while contrast and colour-vision are not. Photophobia/migraine users and low-vision dark-mode users are exactly the population that requests more contrast.
expertFindings.suggested_cure: State contrast level and colour-vision safety as axes orthogonal to polarity, as motion already is (e.g. `data-contrast="more"`, `data-palette="colour-safe"` composing with light/dark), OR require every identity roster to carry dark variants of high-contrast and colour-safe and bind OS signals to the (contrast × polarity) tuple rather than a single theme name. Either way W2.1 must state the composition rule for simultaneous signals and carry a rejection fixture for a manifest whose bindings cannot resolve a dark+more-contrast request.

expertFindings.claim: The stated CSS mechanism cannot deliver its own stated scoping ("an explicit non-system choice wins"), and the runtime half leaves the stored-`system` + contrast-more outcome unspecified — yet both are encoded as new gate cells, so the cells cannot be written unambiguously.
expertFindings.evidence: The light theme is the `:root` default: packages/design/oak-design-system/colors_and_type.css:274 declares every role token at `:root`, while the explicit-light selectors at :559-567 declare ONLY `color-scheme: light`. A `@media (prefers-contrast: more) { :root { …high-contrast roles… } }` block placed after :274 therefore wins for every role token even when the user has explicitly chosen light — an explicit light choice would render high-contrast. Media queries add no specificity. Separately, oak-theme.ts:95-97 `get()` returns `current || stored() || auto() || 'light'`, so a stored `'system'` short-circuits `auto()`; the plan says to "consult `auto()` when the stored choice is `system`" without saying what is applied — applying `high-contrast` discards the user's system dark polarity (see the polarity-lock finding), keeping `system` discards the contrast request.
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Scope the CSS fallback `html:not([data-theme])` (the runtime always writes the attribute when JS runs, so there is no double-application), and record explicitly that with JS disabled a stored explicit light choice cannot be honoured — this contradicts the kit's documented "An explicit user choice always wins" commitment (oak-theme.ts:12-13) and needs a dated note there. State the stored-`system` + contrast-more resolution as a named outcome. Add a third gate cell: explicit `light` + `emulateMedia contrast:more` asserts the LIGHT role values still paint.

expertFindings.section: W2.5(ii)-(iii) (per-identity gate matrix, pinned cell count) + W4.2 (instrument inventory)
expertFindings.claim: Pinning the expected browser cell count at `identities × themes` ratchets coverage DOWN below what is landed today, and W4.2's named instrument inventory omits two cell classes that exist in the suite being rewritten — so they can vanish without any gate noticing.
expertFindings.evidence: demos/oak-design-showcase/tests/showcase-a11y.spec.ts currently runs, beyond identity × theme (:137-153): `prefers-contrast: more` auto-select (:24-32), `forced-colors` renderability (:34-42), focus-ring SC 1.4.11 measure on the switchboard AND on the inverted footer band (:99-135), identity × system under an emulated dark OS (:155-166), and 320px reflow per identity (:168-196). W4.2's inventory names "ring-contrast tool, 320px reflow probe, forced-colours cell, JS-disabled shell, identity × theme axe matrix, the hydration-geometry and load-then-swap invariants" — the `prefers-contrast` auto-select cell and the identity × system (dark OS) cells appear nowhere in the plan's inventory, and the inverted-band ring cell (which guards a hand-measured 1.12:1 regression per the spec's own comment at :123-126) is not distinguished from the switchboard one.
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Define the pinned count as the product over ALL declared axes (identity × theme × OS-signal emulation set), not identity × theme; add the `prefers-contrast` auto-select cell, the identity × system-under-dark-OS cells, and the inverted-band ring cell to W4.2's named inventory by file and test title so the re-point is verifiable line by line.

expertFindings.claim: One specimen-carrier page "carrying every component class once" measures default states only. Interactive, error, disabled, expanded and selected states are where SC 1.4.3, 1.4.11 and 4.1.2 actually fail, and the kit defines distinct tokens for exactly those states. The carrier's status against W4.1's "specimen-primary surfaces FAIL the coverage matrix by definition" is also unstated.
expertFindings.evidence: packages/design/oak-design-system/colors_and_type.css:318-319 `--bg-btn-disabled` / `--text-btn-disabled`, :321-334 correct/incorrect/success/error backgrounds and borders, :678-683 `--focus-ring` / `--focus-ring-inverted` — none of these paint on a component in its default state. components.css:1077-1079 gives `.oak-quiz-answer--selected` a forced-colors-specific border width, and :1083-1088 gives `[data-theme='high-contrast']` tag/chip borders — state-and-theme-specific rules that a default-state carrier never exercises. The existing suite already knows this: the ring contrast measure is a separate keyboard-driven step (showcase-a11y.spec.ts:99-135) precisely because axe ships no focus-indicator rule.
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Require the carrier to render each component class in each of its declared state variants (a state matrix per class, derived from the W0.1 feature census's modifier classes), and to be walked with keyboard focus so `:focus-visible` states are measured. State explicitly that the carrier is a test fixture outside the wow bar and outside W4.5's coverage matrix, so W4.1's specimen-primary prohibition does not collide with it.

expertFindings.claim: W0.6 states "RED comes from the missing assertions, never from missing product behaviour", but the hub has never been axe-tested and ADR-147 is zero-tolerance — so the plan carries no disposition for the realistic outcome that the new suite goes red on real hub defects, and the "hub stays as-is" ruling is not scoped to exclude accessibility defects.
expertFindings.evidence: demos/oak-curriculum-hub/package.json has no `test:ui` and no `test:a11y` script (verified: scripts are dev/build/clean/start/type-check/lint/lint:fix/test/test:watch plus tool:*); .github/workflows/ci.yml:230 runs `turbo run test:e2e test:ui test:a11y test:widget`, so the hub contributes nothing to that leg today. W0.2(a) only covers "every existing design gate", which the hub has none of. The plan's own §Cross-demo records 548 arbitrary-value occurrences in the hub as accepted standing debt — arbitrary colour utilities are precisely the mechanism by which a pairing escapes the token contrast gate, so the hub's contrast is covered by nothing except the axe cells W0.6 lands.
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Give W0.6 an explicit remediation branch: violations found are triaged like W0.2(b) KNOWN-ISSUES accessibility entries (fix-only, never `skipRules`), with the fix stories named as W0 work rather than deferred; and state in the charter that the hub's as-is ruling covers architecture and consumption path only, never accessibility defects. Record the hub's arbitrary-value debt as an a11y risk (untokenised colour is ungated colour), not only a token-discipline debt.

expertFindings.claim: "Reduced motion = motion tokens collapse to the floor per the kit's `data-motion` semantics" is not enforceable in the Tailwind showcase: `data-motion` only re-points custom properties, and Tailwind's motion and transform utility families are caught by neither of the plan's two detectors.
expertFindings.evidence: packages/design/oak-design-system/colors_and_type.css:511-521 — `[data-motion='reduced']` and `[data-motion='full']` re-point only `--motion-quick/base/loop`; nothing reaches a declaration that does not read those variables. W4.6's stated check is "`-\[` pattern in JSX class strings, plus role-name resolution for colour/spacing utilities" — `duration-300`, `animate-pulse`, `transition-all`, `ease-in-out` and `rotate-3` are neither arbitrary values nor colour/spacing utilities, so they pass. (The CSS-side detector does cover durations — demos/oak-design-showcase/tools/css-literal-values.unit.test.ts:25 asserts `transition-duration: 200ms` is reported — which makes the JSX-side gap the asymmetry.) `rotate-*` matters twice over: W2.7's off-horizontal work is a transform axis and would escape the same check.
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Extend the W4.6 check to the motion and transform utility families (`transition-*`, `duration-*`, `delay-*`, `ease-*`, `animate-*`, `rotate-*`, `skew-*`), requiring them to resolve to mapped role names. Add a rendered assertion to the cross-demo cells: under `emulateMedia({ reducedMotion: 'reduce' })` and under `data-motion="reduced"`, computed `transition-duration` and `animation-name` on a named sample of animated elements read as collapsed — in every demo, not only the ones whose CSS is authored by hand.

expertFindings.claim: The DoD is made normative and becomes the ceiling, but omits SC 2.4.11 Focus Not Obscured (Minimum) — a WCAG 2.2 AA criterion that no automated tool checks and that the showcase's own sticky identity/theme switchboard is the textbook failure pattern for — along with the manual-review criteria generally.
expertFindings.evidence: The enumerated DoD is "forced-colours cell with the matchMedia gate, 320px reflow, 400% zoom, target-size at the kit's 44px floor, skip link, `lang`, text-spacing". Live W3C Understanding SC 2.4.11 (fetched 2026-08-02): Level AA; typical failure patterns are sticky headers/footers and persistent user-opened panels that fully hide the focused component. docs/governance/accessibility-practice.md:28 already lists 2.4.11 as a key criterion, so the DoD is narrower than the governing practice doc it must satisfy. Also absent: SC 2.4.3 Focus Order / 1.3.2 Meaningful Sequence (which W4.2 relies on), 1.4.13 Content on Hover or Focus (named in W3.1 for components but not at page level), 2.5.7 Dragging Movements, and any reduced-motion cell. The kit's own CLAUDE.md holds AA as the floor with AAA as the aspiration, which an enumerated ceiling quietly inverts.
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Add 2.4.11 with a concrete cell (tab through every page with the switchboard sticky; assert the focused element's rect is not fully covered by any fixed/sticky element), plus 2.4.3/1.3.2, 1.4.13 and 2.5.7. State the enumeration as a floor with a named manual-review pass (the W0.7 accessibility-expert leg) covering the criteria axe cannot reach — axe covers roughly 30-40% of WCAG failures, so an enumerated automatable list read as complete is a conformance over-claim.

expertFindings.section: W4.3 (a11y trio generated from gate report artefacts)
expertFindings.claim: Generating the a11y trio's "guarantee/obligation content FROM the gate's own report artefacts" cannot work for half the charter and turns the other half into a conformance over-claim: CI measures only the automatable subset, and the charter's second half is explicitly the part CI does not measure.
expertFindings.evidence: packages/design/oak-design-system/studio-source/preview/a11y-charter.html has exactly two H2s: "The system guarantees" and "Every build must still" — the second is the manual obligations half, which no axe or contrast-manifest artefact produces. The token gate is enumerated, not exhaustive: packages/design/oak-design-tokens/src/design-system-expectations.ts:67 pins 42 declared pairs against :89's 167 resolved colour comparands per composed theme, so a generated "guarantees" page sourced from it describes 42 checked pairings, not the palette. docs/governance/accessibility-practice.md:51-53 states plainly that the tags cover "the automatable subset" and "Manual review remains necessary".
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Generate only the measured half, and require the generated block to carry its own scope statement: which pairings, which axe tags, which identity × theme cells, at which dated commit. Keep "Every build must still" authored, and add the inverse check the finding actually needs — every claim in the guarantees half resolves to a report row (a claim with no measurement fails the build), rather than deriving the prose from the reports.

expertFindings.section: W3.3 (pre-paint identity bootstrap) + W6.1 (cross-demo observable form)
expertFindings.claim: W3.3 promises identity renders on reload/deep-link "without a flash of Oak" but names no mechanism for getting identity CSS into the document before paint, and W6.1's observable — attributes present on the document element — cannot falsify a flash, because Playwright reads attributes after load in every case.
expertFindings.evidence: Identity today is delivered as separate brand stylesheets (packages/design/oak-design-system/studio-source/whitelabel/{creature,freedonia}/brand-a.css, brand-full.css), and the landed showcase already treats identity switching as a runtime sheet load — demos/oak-design-showcase/tests/showcase.spec.ts:155-156 guards "switching between counter-brands never shows the Oak base", i.e. the load-then-swap hazard is known and real. A pre-paint attribute alone does not fetch a stylesheet; if the identity sheet is fetched after hydration, the Oak base paints first regardless of the attribute. W0.3's pre-paint mechanisms are stated per demo for theme only. For the population this protects (photophobia, vestibular, low-vision), a wrong-palette first paint is the harm, not a wrong attribute.
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Name the delivery mechanism: all identity sheets present in the initial HTML and selected by attribute, or the identity resolved server-side from a cookie so the correct sheet is in the first response. Replace the W6.1 observable with one that can fail: a first-frame capture (CDP screencast or a throttled-route screenshot) asserting no frame paints the base palette, in addition to the attribute assertion — and state the same for theme, since attribute-presence has the identical blindness there.

expertFindings.section: W2.2 (declared identity CSS layer) + W0.8 (literal instruments re-homed)
expertFindings.claim: The "declared, bounded identity CSS layer (permitted selector shapes only)" is bounded by selector shape but not by value discipline, and W0.8 derives the literal walker's roster from the demo workspace inventory — so colour authored in an identity layer sits outside both the token-pair contrast gate and the literal walker.
expertFindings.evidence: W2.5(i) gates "the identity's emitted token projection + pairings manifest"; anything declared directly in the identity CSS layer is not in the emitted projection and so is never a comparand. W0.8 states the roster is "derived from the workspace inventory" so "W1/W5's new workspaces are covered by construction" — identity directories under design-tokens-core are not demo workspaces. The only remaining net is the rendered axe run, which reaches an identity-layer colour only where the specimen carrier happens to paint it. The detector already exists and is value-aware (demos/oak-design-showcase/tools/css-literal-values.ts:206 `findLiteralDesignValues`).
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Require the identity CSS layer to be value-free — `var(--role)` references only — and add the identity directories to W0.8's walker roster explicitly, red-proven on a planted hex in an identity layer. That keeps every identity colour inside the projection the contrast matrix actually measures.

expertFindings.claim: "The missing dark-link-on-lemon pairing joins `dtcg/contrast-pairings.json`" adds the measurement but not the cure; the pairing measures 4.48:1 and will fail the AA floor on arrival, so W0.2's "all green" acceptance is unreachable as written.
expertFindings.evidence: packages/design/oak-design-system/KNOWN-ISSUES.md item 13: "Dark-lemon (`#645811`) is the one base it cannot clear: 4.48:1, gate-measured", with the current mitigation being documentation only ("Don't put body links inside a lemon band in dark"). W0.2(b) rules accessibility-class entries fix-only under ADR-147 zero-tolerance, so documentation-as-mitigation is not an available disposition. packages/design/oak-design-tokens/src/design-system-expectations.ts:67 pins `EXPECTED_MANIFEST_PAIR_COUNT = 42`, so adding a pair without re-baselining fails the shape gate too.
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Name the token cure in W0.2(b): either re-point `--text-link` within the decorative-5 band scope in dark, or lift `--oak-dark-lemon` — and state that lifting a shared decorative base re-runs every pairing that consumes it, so the change carries a full re-audit. Add the pair-count re-baseline (42 → 43) to the same acceptance line.

expertFindings.claim: The forced-colours obligation is stated as a single "cell with the matchMedia gate", but under `forced-colors: active` the one surface an identity can still paint — decorative background images — is never contrast-measured by any tool, and the kit has no `forced-color-adjust` policy at all.
expertFindings.evidence: Verified: zero occurrences of `forced-color-adjust` in packages/design/oak-design-system/*.css and in the whitelabel brand sheets. colors_and_type.css:713 applies `background-image: var(--surface-page-image)` to `html, body`; brand.css:174 documents `--surface-page-image` as "page-glow gradients behind everything", i.e. an identity-facing lever. Forced colours replaces `background-color` but not `background-image`, and axe measures text against background-color only — so an identity page image under forced colours can render text unreadable with no gate reacting. The landed forced-colours assertion is renderability only (demos/oak-design-showcase/tests/showcase-a11y.spec.ts:34-42: an H1 is visible).
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Add a forced-colours obligation to the identity contract: decorative background images and gradients suppress under `forced-colors: active` (or carry an explicit `forced-color-adjust` decision), meaning-bearing chrome uses system colour keywords, and the transparent-outline focus pattern is preserved. Strengthen the cell from renderability to a computed check that `--surface-page-image` resolves to `none` per identity in that mode.

expertFindings.claim: The plan's own TDD-compliance claim is false: it states "Each story below names its describing surface and first RED (E47)", but only 3 of 40 stories name a describing surface. E47's row in dispositions.v2.md records "applied — Every story names describing surface + first RED", so the ledger the re-review fleet reads mis-reports the cure.
expertFindings.evidence: grep over <repo>/.agent/plans/delivery/design-system-completion.plan.md: 40 story bullets (`^- \*\*W[0-9]`); "Describing surface" appears at lines 164 (W0.1), 303 (W2.1), 407 (W3.1) only. Any RED-shaped phrase appears in ~12 story lines. W0.3, W0.4, W0.5, W1.1, W1.2, W2.2, W2.4, W2.5, W2.7–W2.10, W3.0, W3.2–W3.4, W4.1–W4.5, W5.1–W5.4, W6.1–W6.4 name neither. tdd-as-design.md §One State, One Describing Surface: "The cure fires at plan-author time... state the describing surface in one sentence before the cycle decomposition is settled, and tag each cycle's test boundary against it."
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Either add the one-sentence describing surface + first RED to every story (cheap: most already imply it), or state one describing surface per workstream in the workstream preamble and tag each story's test boundary against it — then correct E47's disposition row to `absorbed-with-correction` naming what was actually applied. Untagged stories default to scaffolding tests per tdd-as-design §One State, One Describing Surface.

expertFindings.claim: The identity-№N falsifier — the mechanical form of the strategic node's falsifiability claim — has no stated rendering mechanism, and as written it contradicts W4.3's shipped-surface assertion. W2.6 requires a synthetic identity fixture "living outside the framework's importable tree" yet "rendered in the same identity × theme matrix"; W2.5's rendered leg is a specimen-carrier page inside the showcase build; W3.3 makes the demo's identity list "config-driven... (no hardcoded union)". If the fixture is reachable by the demo's config it appears in the shipped identity control and W4.3's "Identity control on every page offers exactly the three configured identities" goes red; if it is not, nothing can render it. Neither branch is red-then-green provable as specified.
expertFindings.evidence: Plan lines 342–348 (W2.6), 419–425 (W3.3), 458–465 (W4.3), 330–336 (W2.5). Verified first-hand that today's matrix is driven by a hand-written literal list in the demo's own test helper: <repo>/demos/oak-design-showcase/tests/apply-state.ts:21 `export const IDENTITIES = ['oak', 'freedonia', 'creature'] as const;` — so "rendered in the same matrix" today means editing that list, i.e. exactly the edit the falsifier forbids. Injecting the fixture via ambient build state would additionally hit test-immediate-fails #5/#16 (env reads; fixtures varying with ambient state).
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Name the fixture surface in W2.6: a test-only fixture app/route (demos-tier, excluded from shipped builds and from W4.5's demonstrating-surface set) built from a fixture manifest directory that the falsifier drops a manifest into; assert the axes on that surface. Then restate W4.3's criterion as "the shipped identity control offers exactly the three owner-named identities (oak, emc2, freedonia) by literal name" so the two gates cannot collide, and per testing-patterns §Discriminating Fixtures pick a fixture whose axis values differ observably from Oak's on every axis (a value that would still pass under a broken emitter is not a tripwire).

expertFindings.claim: The theme-№N falsifier is unachievable under the implementation the same story permits, and its consumer census is undercounted — including one consumer outside the plan's declared scope.
