W2.3 allows the five lists to "derive from it OR are build-checked against it"; a build-checked list still requires a hand edit to mint theme №N, which directly falsifies the acceptance criterion "a config-minted test theme reaches `data-theme`, the matrix, and the labels with zero list edits".
expertFindings.evidence: Plan lines 313–321. First-hand grep for the theme literal shows more hand-maintained lists than the plan's five: packages/design/oak-design-system/src/oak-theme.ts:31,48; packages/design/oak-design-react/src/oak-theme-store.ts:39; packages/design/oak-design-tokens/src/design-system-expectations.ts:15,28,54 (three separate maps: names, per-theme WCAG levels, per-theme semantic roots); packages/design/oak-design-tokens/src/design-system-contrast.ts:57,63; demos/oak-design-showcase/tests/apply-state.ts:22,51; demos/oak-design-showcase/components/Switchboard.tsx:42 and Switchboard.unit.test.tsx:21; demos/oak-curriculum-hub/components/ThemeSwitcher.tsx:23 and ThemeSwitcher.test.tsx:28; and apps/oak-curriculum-mcp-streamable-http/tests/visual/apply-theme.ts:4 — a theme matrix in a workspace the plan's §In scope does not cover.
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Drop the "or are build-checked against it" disjunct (build-checking cannot satisfy a zero-edit falsifier). Replace the hand-enumerated list of five with a mechanical consumer census: a validator that fails when any literal theme-name array/record exists outside the generated roster module (the same shape as the existing validate-authored-css walker, including its zero-files non-vacuity leg). Add an explicit disposition for apps/oak-curriculum-mcp-streamable-http/tests/visual/apply-theme.ts — in scope, or an owner-accepted exclusion recorded in §Out of scope.

expertFindings.claim: The census is the ground truth for the whole exit checklist, yet nothing falsifies UNDER-enumeration. Its acceptance is "both artefacts committed with zero undispositioned rows" and its only stated RED runs the other way ("generator asserts a census entry the walk cannot find"). A feature the generator never sees is not an undispositioned row — it is no row at all, so W4.5's matrix and W6.4's "zero undispositioned deltas" are green by omission. W6.4 also compares census to census by the same generator, which testing-patterns §Acceptance Value-Proxies rejects as tautological.
expertFindings.evidence: Plan lines 152–168 (W0.1), 477–482 (W4.5), 536–538 (W6.4). Independent ground truths exist and are cheap: `find . -name '*.html'` under packages/design/oak-open-curriculum-design-system-tna-24072026-1141 = 81 (matching the plan's stated 81), and `grep -oE '\.oak-[a-z0-9-]+' packages/design/oak-design-system/components.css | sort -u | wc -l` = 104 distinct component classes. Neither count is named as a parity check in the plan.
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Make W0.1's describing tests bidirectional: a planted class/page/token-root in a fixture tree MUST appear in the generated census (RED = it does not), alongside the existing declared-but-absent case. Add a parity acceptance line binding each census axis to a method-independent count (export page-file count; distinct `.oak-` class count from components.css; token-root count from the canonical CSS) per testing-patterns §Acceptance Value-Proxies, and have W6.4 re-run the parity legs rather than only diffing census-to-census.

expertFindings.claim: Two stories specify validator-shaped work as unit tests, which the estate's own recipes forbid. W0.1 names "the census generator's unit tests" with a RED that runs the walk; W3.4 names "a module-level assertion test over the tier's exports" to prove presentational components carry no `'use client'`. Both assert repo/source state through the vitest harness — filesystem IO in a unit test (test-immediate-fails #4/#20) and the exact shape recipes call "a validator wearing a vitest harness".
expertFindings.evidence: Plan lines 164–166 and 427–430. docs/engineering/testing-tdd-recipes.md §Validator Script vs Integration Test: "if the test body is readdirSync / existsSync / readFileSync over real repo paths and assertions are about repo state (not function output), it belongs in scripts/... not in the test runner." The estate already has the conformant precedent in this exact area: demos/oak-design-showcase/tools/css-literal-values.ts (pure classifier, unit-tested at css-literal-values.unit.test.ts) plus tools/validate-authored-css.ts (standalone script doing the walk).
expertFindings.suggested_cure: State the split in both stories: pure classifier (rows in → dispositioned census out; module record in → boundary verdict out) with `*.unit.test.ts`, plus a workspace-owned script performing the walk and wired into `pnpm check`, citing the css-literal-values/validate-authored-css precedent. For W3.4 prefer the observable form instead — an ESLint boundary rule for the directive, and a render-level assertion that the showcase page/layout produce no client bundle — since a directive-presence assertion is audit-shaped (it constrains how, not what).

expertFindings.claim: The coverage matrix binds census rows to "assertion ids" with no mechanism for resolving an id to a live, executed, passing test and no orphan leg. As written the gate can go green while an id points at a renamed, moved or deleted test — a recording surface, not a validator.
expertFindings.evidence: Plan lines 477–482: "the gate fails when (a) a census entry has no demonstrating surface and (b) a demonstrating surface carries no passing assertion id — each row bound to a named test." No source of "passing" is named (test-runner report, reporter format), and no failure is specified for an id that resolves to zero tests. .agent/rules/validators-must-recompute-not-just-record.md: "A validator that only records the value, never compares it, is a recording surface, not a validation surface."
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Name the mechanism in the acceptance line: the matrix gate consumes the runners' JSON reports (vitest + Playwright) produced by the same `pnpm check` run, and fails on (i) census row with no id, (ii) id resolving to zero executed tests (orphan), (iii) id resolving to a non-passing test, (iv) an executed test whose id is in no row (unbound), with a zero-tests-scanned non-vacuity leg mirroring validate-authored-css's zero-files failure.

expertFindings.claim: The ADR-147 gate extension for `oak-design-react` is sequenced in W2, before W3.1's first component exists, so its acceptance ("the extended gate green on the tier package") is satisfiable vacuously: per-theme axe runs, a forced-colours render check and motion-axis coverage over a package that renders nothing all pass by construction.
expertFindings.evidence: Plan lines 374–378 (W2.10 in W2; "The HARD gate on W3's first component export") and §Sequencing line 578 (W2 → W3). Verified first-hand: `ls packages/design/oak-design-react/src` returns only index.ts, oak-theme-store.ts, oak-theme-store.unit.test.ts — the tier exports no components today, and its package.json has no test:ui/test:a11y script.
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Either land the gate in the same PR as W3.1's first component family (atomic-landing invariant — the gate and the surface it describes are one act), or add a non-vacuity acceptance leg: the gate fails when the rendered component roster is empty and when the roster count differs from the tier's exported component surface, plus a one-off red proof against a planted violation (per testing-strategy §Prove the guard bites).

expertFindings.claim: Three stories land tests against already-green behaviour with no substitute for the RED phase. W0.6 states outright that "RED comes from the missing assertions, never from missing product behaviour" — that is not a red phase: such a suite passes on first run and can be written to mirror whatever the hub currently does (audit-shaped by construction). None of the three carries the mutation-bite acceptance that W2.1/W2.6 do, and W0.2(a)'s red-gate fixes carry no defect-test obligation.
expertFindings.evidence: Plan lines 226–233 (W0.6), 518–526 (W6.1 hub "story is VERIFICATION of its existing wiring"), 169–176 (W0.2(a) "red gates are fixed before anything else", acceptance is only "all green with evidence linked"). testing-strategy.md §Prove the guard bites: "Any test added to close a proof gap is validated by MUTATING the source to the wrong behaviour and confirming exactly that test fails"; §When a Defect Is Found: "write the test that reproduces the defect (Red) BEFORE the fix, at the same level... Describe the class the defect generalises to."
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Add to W0.6 and W6.1's hub leg an acceptance line requiring a recorded mutation proof per assertion group (mutate the hub's pre-paint bootstrap / theme write and confirm exactly the new cell fails), and to W0.2(a) the defect-test obligation: each red gate is cured by a reproducing test at the defective scale landing in the same commit as the fix, generalised to the defect class.

expertFindings.claim: The "named inventory" of instruments to re-point when the rejected showcase page is deleted is hand-written in the plan and is demonstrably incomplete against the live suites, so specs will be silently dropped at the migration landings while the acceptance line ("the instrument inventory accounted") reads green.
expertFindings.evidence: Plan lines 443–456 names: ring-contrast tool, 320px reflow probe, forced-colours cell, JS-disabled shell, identity × theme axe matrix, hydration-geometry and load-then-swap invariants. First-hand enumeration of demos/oak-design-showcase/tests/showcase.spec.ts additionally contains: 'a theme choice survives reload through the pre-paint bootstrap' (:74), 'no-choice reads as Page default and the first Light choice bites' (:84), 'an OS contrast request themes the page without claiming a choice' (:100), 'a reduced-motion choice collapses the motion tokens' (:112), 'the dark-first counter-brand is dark with no theme chosen' (:138), 'system matches the explicit dark palette under a dark OS' (:217), plus 'serves the showcase under the region contract' (:36). Four co-located unit suites also describe the deleted surface: app/page.unit.test.tsx, components/Switchboard.unit.test.tsx, components/LabelledSelect.unit.test.tsx, lib/inline-script.unit.test.ts, and tools/kit-asset-parity.unit.test.ts is unnamed anywhere in the plan.
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Replace the hand list with a generated one, matching W0.1/W4.5's own discipline: at the first migration landing, enumerate every test that resolves against the deleted surface (`playwright test --list --reporter=json` plus the co-located `*.unit.test.*` files under the deleted modules) into a committed inventory artefact with one disposition per row (retained verbatim / re-expressed / dropped with reason), and make W4.2's acceptance "zero undispositioned rows in the generated inventory".

expertFindings.claim: "Resolved theme + motion attributes present on the document element BEFORE first paint" is presented as the mechanical cross-demo criterion for all four demos, but no observable is named and the estate has no such assertion today. The predictable implementation is a post-load attribute assertion, which passes even when the page flashes — the exact defect the criterion exists to exclude.
expertFindings.evidence: Plan lines 518–526 and 541–544. First-hand: demos/oak-design-showcase/tests/showcase.spec.ts:74–79 asserts `data-theme` after `page.reload()` (post-load), and the only pre-paint-adjacent proof is the JS-disabled geometry parity check in tests/apply-state.ts:117–150 (`measureSwitchboardGeometry`). No test in the workspace observes attribute state at paint time.
expertFindings.suggested_cure: State two observables in W6.1: (i) a structural assertion over the served HTML text — the bootstrap is a parser-blocking element in `<head>` preceding any body content (deterministic, no browser needed); and (ii) a runtime capture via `page.addInitScript` recording `document.documentElement.getAttribute('data-theme')`/`data-motion` while `document.readyState === 'loading'`, asserted equal to the resolved value. Keep the JS-disabled shell cell as the third leg.

expertFindings.claim: The styled-components demo has no described surface. W5 specifies workspace plumbing, tier consumption and token discipline, then an owner-held wow checkpoint (W5.4) with no stated page set and no repo-safe acceptance for content — so "wow" has no object, and no census row can bind to this demo. W1 (three composed pages) and W4.1 (named page set) both do this correctly.
expertFindings.evidence: Plan lines 493–514: W5.1 acceptance "`pnpm check` from cold; the first-paint assertion"; W5.2 "demo suites; zero forked component copies"; W5.3 "detector red-proven; suites green"; W5.4 "Wow checkpoint (`owner-held`)" with no body. Contrast W1.2 ("The export's three composed pages, authored fresh against the live kit") and W4.1 ("the page-set artefact the matrix derives from").
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Add a W5.x story naming the styled demo's page set (seeded from the census `express-composed` rows, as W4.1 does), with its describing surface (Playwright cells per page + the demos-tier a11y DoD) and its rows in the W4.5 matrix, so W5.4's checkpoint has a defined object and the demo's coverage is on the same exit checklist as the others.

expertFindings.claim: Browser-requiring accessibility criteria are assigned to the component families' unit tests. W3.1's describing surface is "unit tests + the fixtures-parity file", yet the same bullet demands keyboard-model tests for focus trap and return, roving tabindex, and SC 1.4.13 dismissal. In a jsdom/happy-dom unit test these can only be simulated (no real focus-visible, no layout, no hover), producing green tests that describe the simulation rather than the behaviour.
expertFindings.evidence: Plan lines 400–409. The showcase's precedent puts exactly these judgements in the browser: demos/oak-design-showcase/tests/showcase-a11y.spec.ts:99–136 walks real Tab presses and reads computed box-shadow for the SC 1.4.11 verdict; the tier package has no DOM test environment at all today (packages/design/oak-design-react/package.json scripts: build, type-check, test, lint only).
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Split the criteria in W3.1: unit tests describe pure prop→kit-class mapping and the fixtures-parity equivalence; keyboard, focus-trap/return, and SC 1.4.13 dismissal move to W2.10's Playwright gate on the tier package (per component family, per theme), which is where the plan already puts the tier's rendered a11y runs. tdd-as-design §Why Scales Are Complementary — the scales are complementary, not substitutional.

expertFindings.claim: W2.5's rendered a11y leg requires "ONE specimen-carrier page per identity × theme carrying every component class once" while W4.1 rules that "a surface whose primary content is the feature itself (a specimen grid) FAILS the coverage matrix by definition", with the bounded exception limited to the reference tier. The carrier is a specimen grid and is not in the exception, and the owner's recorded taste calibration REJECTED bare specimen grids — so the a11y matrix's carrier is either an owner-facing surface that fails the wow bar and the matrix, or an unstated test-only surface.
expertFindings.evidence: Plan lines 330–336 (W2.5), 437–442 (W4.1), 88–92 (taste calibration: "REJECTED — bare specimen grids").
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Declare the specimen carrier in W2.5 as a test-only fixture route (not linked from the shipped navigation, excluded from wow checkpoints and from W4.5's demonstrating-surface set), and state explicitly that census rows may NOT claim the carrier as their demonstrating surface — otherwise every component class could satisfy the exit checklist from the grid the owner rejected.

expertFindings.claim: The composition focus-order check is specified as "assert sequential focus order matches visual order (`getBoundingClientRect` monotonicity)" with no reading-order model. Monotonic rect comparison is wrong for wrapped, multi-column and CSS-reordered layouts — precisely the compositions the owner's re-ordering requirement makes central — so the cell will either produce false reds or grow branching logic inside the Playwright test (test-immediate-fails #14: no non-trivial functions in tests).
expertFindings.evidence: Plan lines 449–455. The estate already carries the correct shape for this class of judgement: demos/oak-design-showcase/tests/showcase-a11y.spec.ts:45–49 states it explicitly — "Every judgement (layer split, alpha compositing, adjacency-chain contrast) lives in tools/focus-ring-contrast.ts, unit-tested with literal fixtures — this helper only observes."
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Name a pure reading-order comparator (rect list + writing mode → verdict) living beside the demo's tools, unit-tested over literal rect fixtures including a wrapped grid and an intentionally CSS-reordered variant; the Playwright cell only collects rects and asserts the comparator's verdict, following the focus-ring-contrast precedent.

expertFindings.claim: The design-review instrument's calibration is a one-off ("red-then-green calibration, run once at landing"), so after any rubric edit the instrument's fail state is unfalsifiable — the must-fail reference (the rejected page) is never re-checked. This contradicts the standing-falsifier discipline the plan applies elsewhere.
expertFindings.evidence: Plan lines 234–244 (W0.7) versus line 348 (W2.6 acceptance: "all fixtures standing in CI, each proven biting by mutation once") and dispositions.v2.md X22: "W2.6 — standing CI falsifiers, mutation-proven once, never one-off".
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Bind re-calibration to rubric revision: the committed calibration record names the rubric revision it calibrated, and any change to the rubric requires a re-run recorded in the same PR (an acceptance line of whatever story edits the rubric). If the instrument is judgement-based and unsuitable for CI, say so explicitly and keep it as an on-demand instrument with the revision-bound calibration record as its guard.

expertFindings.section: delivery plan — W0.1 (page census) and §In scope / owner requirement 4
expertFindings.claim: The plan's load-bearing page census — "the export's 81 page artefacts … (verified 2026-08-02: 62 preview/, 3 top-level composed pages, 4 components/, 3 templates/, 5 whitelabel/, ui_kits/oak, thumbnail, integrations, docs)" — enumerates the ARCHIVED original capture, not the live export, and names no tree by path. Executing W0.1's mechanical walk over the live tree contradicts the plan's own stated figure, and owner requirement 4 ("ALL pages from the design system export") resolves against an unnamed, ambiguous referent.
expertFindings.evidence: First-hand counts (2026-08-02, working tree): `packages/design/oak-design-system/studio-source/original-capture-2026-07-23/` contains exactly 81 `.html` files, broken down 62 preview + 3 top-level + `thumbnail.html` + 4 components + 3 templates + 5 whitelabel + 1 ui_kits + 1 integrations + 1 docs = 81 — an item-for-item match with the plan's list, including `thumbnail` and `docs`, which exist ONLY in that capture tree. The LIVE `studio-source/` tree has 79 `.html` (62 preview + 3 top-level + 4 components + 3 templates + 5 whitelabel + 1 ui_kits + 1 integrations); it has no `thumbnail.html`, and the kit's single docs page (`packages/design/oak-design-system/docs/headless-a11y-frameworks.html`) sits outside `studio-source/` entirely. Total `.html` under `studio-source/` is 168 (79 live + 81 capture + 8 `iteration-pull-preservation-2026-07-23/`). Three further full export copies exist in-repo with different counts: `packages/design/oak-open-curriculum-design-system-tna-24072026-1141` (81), `packages/design/design-import` (82), `ds-bundle` (1).
expertFindings.suggested_cure: In W0.1 name the census domain by path (`packages/design/oak-design-system/studio-source/`, excluding `original-capture-2026-07-23/` and `iteration-pull-preservation-2026-07-23/`) and state the archive rule explicitly: the preservation trees are historical records, never the requirement's domain. Delete the pre-stated "81" (or restate it as the capture tree's count, labelled as such) so the generated artefact is the only authority for the number, and carry the same domain statement into the Demos Charter so the wow-coverage claim has one resolvable page set.

expertFindings.claim: v2 does not "drop the re-wrap mandate" — it adopts the shape ADR-213 §3 names as rejected, for every component in the tier, with no amendment. The verdict that "the §3 rejection stands unamended" is therefore doctrinally unsound, and the dispositions ledger records E14/E66 as cured on a premise the v2 text contradicts.
expertFindings.evidence: Plan W3.1: "the seed components REWRITTEN at adoption (E20) — consume kit classes (`.oak-btn`, `.oak-tag`, …) with variants as props … no `style` prop"; W4.6 and §Decision log restate it ("Tier components paint via kit classes"). ADR-213 §3 Standing rules: "**Re-wrapping the class library in a framework component layer remains rejected** (it would fork the tier-3 contract). This question is settled here and is not re-litigated per widget", reaffirmed by the 2026-07-23 amendment under "Stands unchanged": "the tier-3 token contract (owned components consume tier-3 tokens identically to the class library — the invariant the re-wrap rejection protects; the rejection of re-wrapping the _class library itself_ in a component layer therefore also stands)". The corpus embodies the peer-consumer reading first-hand: `packages/design/oak-design-system/studio-source/components/OakButton/OakButton.jsx` opens "Consumes the SAME tier-3 tokens as .oak-btn in components.css, so class library and bundle cannot drift" and paints via inline `var(--btn-*)` values, never a kit class; ADR-213 §Context describes "tier-3 component tokens consumed identically by a `.oak-*` class library and four compiled React components". `dispositions.v2.md` E14/E66 assert "no re-wrap mandate remains, so the §3 rejection stands unamended".
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Make the ADR-213 §3 dated amendment an acceptance line of W3.0 (which already carries the §3 landing-sequence set): record that adopted components paint via kit recipe classes, state what the re-wrap rejection now protects (one recipe definition, no forked tier-3 contract), and supersede the "components consume tier-3 tokens identically to the class library" clause in the same edit. Alternatively restate W3.1 as peer tier-3 consumption. Either way the §3 reading must live in the ADR, not only in the plan's Decision log.

expertFindings.section: W2 preamble / W2.2–W2.5 — ADR-213 §2 dated amendment scope
expertFindings.claim: The §2 identity-configuration amendment is specified without stating whether Oak is inside or outside the new authored-configuration surface. Both readings break something the plan asserts, so the amendment as scoped cannot be written unambiguously.
expertFindings.evidence: Plan W2 preamble: "Oak's base kit keeps the ADR-213 §2 CSS→projection direction; the identity manifest is recorded as a NEW authored configuration surface by a dated §2 amendment (it is identity configuration feeding the framework, never a second Oak token source)". But W2.2 states "Per identity, at ITS migration landing, the emitted CSS replaces the hand-authored sheet (replace-dont-bridge — no identity is served by both)" with no Oak carve-out; W2.3 makes the theme roster "a generated artefact consumed by the kit runtime" whose five hand-maintained lists (incl. the kit's own `src/oak-theme.ts:31` union, verified) derive from it; W2.4/W2.5 run per identity; W4.3 requires the identity control to offer all three configured identities including Oak. If Oak gets a manifest, the plan has created the second Oak token source §2 and ADR-148's invariant forbid; if it does not, the roster generator, the emitter and the per-identity gate matrix have no Oak input and Oak sits outside the very falsifier the strategic node's thesis rests on.
expertFindings.suggested_cure: State Oak's status in W2's preamble and make it a clause of the §2 amendment: e.g. Oak's manifest carries the non-token fields (assets, voice, polarity, roster, OS bindings) and REFERENCES the kit CSS-derived projection for its token block, so no Oak token is authored twice; non-Oak identities author their token block. Add the roster generator's Oak input path explicitly to W2.3.

expertFindings.section: §Relationships (ADR obligations by workstream) / W2.2 — ADR-041 and ADR-213 §4
expertFindings.claim: W2 creates a new producer→consumer relation (an emitter in `design-tokens-core` generating identity CSS the kit and demos consume) but the ADR-obligations map schedules no ADR-041 / ADR-213 §4 dependency-map amendment, and ADR-041 is the authoritative map.
expertFindings.evidence: Plan W2 preamble: "Owning workspace: `design-tokens-core` for schema + validators + emitter; the kit's public surface is unchanged". ADR-041's 2026-07-19/2026-07-20 amendment (`041-workspace-structure-option-a.md` lines 134–170) records "`design-tokens-core` imports nothing from the design tier" and "`oak-design-system` carries NO `design-tokens-core` edge (corrected 2026-07-20 twice)"; ADR-213 §4 repeats it and adds "ADR-041 is the authoritative map". The plan's §Relationships map lists W2.1 → ADR-213 §2 only; W1.1/W5.1 → ADR-041 demos rows only. No entry covers the emitter edge.
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Add to the ADR-obligations map: W2.2 → ADR-041 intra-design amendment + ADR-213 §4 note, either recording the new edge or recording that emission produces an out-of-tree build artefact creating no workspace import edge (with the boundary rule that proves it). Make it an acceptance line of W2.2 alongside the emitter's tests.

expertFindings.claim: W0.3 instructs reducing a section that does not exist, and as written it will reinstate the exact index-carries-content duplication the finding it cures was raised against.
expertFindings.evidence: W0.3: "with `demos/README.md` §Charter reduced to a pointer plus a row-per-demo table", and separately lists "`demos/README.md` §Projects" in the kit-side correction set. First-hand: `demos/README.md` is 50 lines with §Dependency boundary, §Projects, §Licences — there is no §Charter (`grep -rn "[Cc]harter" demos/` returns nothing). §Projects already carries per-demo consumption prose ("consuming the kit the plain-CSS way … with no Tailwind and no mapping layer"). Executed literally, a NEW §Charter table lands beside §Projects' prose — two copies of per-demo consumption facts in one index file, against ADR-127 §5 ("READMEs and index surfaces are APIs: they point, they do not carry") and the DRY clause.
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Rewrite the clause as: "`demos/README.md` gains a one-line §Charter pointer to the ADR amendment, and §Projects' rows are rewritten to name the demo and point at its charter row rather than restating its consumption path" — naming exactly one home for per-demo consumption prose.

expertFindings.section: W0.3 — charter content homed in ADR-213
expertFindings.claim: The charter's payload overloads an already-oversized ADR and forks the accessibility SSOT, including a target-size number that differs from the canonical home's.
expertFindings.evidence: `213-design-system-integration-and-component-architecture.md` is 531 lines carrying the integration contract, licensing, source-of-truth with four dated §2 amendment blocks, the component system with a §3 amendment plus a 2026-08-02 dated amendment, the dependency map, owner gates and alternatives. W0.3 adds to it per-demo pre-paint mechanisms, an "enumerated demos-tier a11y DoD (forced-colours cell with the matchMedia gate, 320px reflow, 400% zoom, target-size at the kit's 44px floor, skip link, `lang`, text-spacing)", a composition rule, an identity-reachability reading and a hub wow reading. Those a11y facts have canonical homes: `docs/governance/accessibility-practice.md:82` already fixes "The gate is `matchMedia('(forced-colors: active)')` — never a …", and :29 records "2.5.8 Target Size (Minimum) — 24×24 CSS pixels" against the charter's "44px floor" — a second copy with a different number. E55's own cure offered "a dated ADR-213 amendment (or a new ADR, per PDR-019)"; the god-document cost of the first option was not weighed.
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Mint a separate ADR for the demos-tier charter (assignment table, per-demo consumption path, pre-paint mechanism, identity reading) and have it cite ADR-213 §3/§4 for what they say. Keep the a11y DoD as a pointer to ADR-147 + `docs/governance/accessibility-practice.md`, with the kit's stricter 44px floor recorded once in the kit's own contract and referenced from both.

expertFindings.section: W0.3 / §Decision log — hub wow reading in the ADR amendment
expertFindings.claim: A clause the plan itself labels a provisional assumption awaiting possible owner overrule is scheduled into a permanent ADR amendment — a moving target in a permanent doc.
expertFindings.evidence: W0.3: the charter carries "the **hub wow reading** (F4/D3): 'as-is' covers architecture and consumption path; the hub sits inside the wow checkpoint like every demo, and a failed checkpoint opens scoped visual-cure work (recorded assumption — the owner can overrule at the first hub checkpoint)"; §Decision log: "Hub wow reading … Seat verdict per F4/D3 — recorded assumption, owner overrules at W6.2". The charter is landed by W0.3 as a dated ADR-213 amendment; W6.2 (the overrule point) is the last workstream.
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Keep the reading in the plan's §Decision log only until W6.2 resolves it, and land the ADR clause afterwards; or state it in the ADR as the decision with the W6.2 checkpoint named as its falsifier, dropping the "recorded assumption / owner can overrule" framing that makes the permanent text provisional.

expertFindings.section: W2.5 / §Relationships — ADR-147 and ADR-121 amendment scope
expertFindings.claim: The scheduled ADR-147/ADR-121 amendments are too narrow: they leave a factually false CI-promotion clause and a permanent-doc-cites-a-plan pointer inside the same documents the plan edits, which W0.6 and W2.10 make more misleading.
expertFindings.evidence: Plan W2.5 lands "the dated ADR-147 §Standard + ADR-121 coverage-matrix amendments (E53)". First-hand: `.github/workflows/ci.yml:230` runs `pnpm exec turbo run test:e2e test:ui test:a11y test:widget`, and ADR-121's matrix row reads `| test:a11y | -- | -- | Yes | Yes |` (CI = Yes). Yet ADR-147 §Tooling still says "Currently enforced in `pnpm check` (local); promotion to pre-push and CI is tracked in the quality gate hardening plan (item 0d)", and ADR-121 §Rationale still says "**Pre-push and CI exclude** test:widget … and test:a11y … Promotion is tracked in the quality gate hardening plan (item 0d)" — contradicting its own matrix. The plan's W0.6 acceptance ("the new suites green in CI at the ci.yml `test:a11y` leg") and W2.10 ("CI promotion of `test:a11y` for the tier package") both rely on the live behaviour these clauses deny.
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Widen both amendments in W2.5: true ADR-147 §Tooling and ADR-121 §Rationale to the landed CI state, and replace the "quality gate hardening plan (item 0d)" pointers with the landed outcome — permanent docs cite outcomes and stable identities, not plan item numbers.

expertFindings.claim: All three owner gates carry multi-paragraph decision narrative in frontmatter against the delivery contract's explicit rule, and the disposition ledger records only the unrelated ratification-timing deviation — so the finding is formally answered while the defect survives into v2's new gates.
expertFindings.evidence: `.agent/plans/plan-node-schema.md:122`: "The body carries (PDR-018: narrative in the body, never frontmatter)". v2 gate 1's `clears_when` runs ten lines including "(v1 conflated the two — corpus E63/X4)"; gate 2 runs nine lines including "(corpus E7/E78: the landed Freedonia is currently the corpus's most orthogonal identity …)"; gate 3 cites "(corpus E11/E31/E32)". E63's original evidence named this explicitly ("`owner_gates[0].clears_when` runs ten lines of decision provenance"), but `dispositions.v2.md` E63 records only the sketch-vs-ratified deviation and asserts the gate "disentangles mint from ratification (the cure's core)".
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Reduce each `clears_when` to one sentence naming the clearing condition, and move the provenance into §Decision log / §Owner rulings in the body. Correct E63's ledger row so the re-review fleet can see which half was applied and which deviates.

expertFindings.section: delivery plan — whole body, review-corpus citations
expertFindings.claim: The plan's grounds are carried by ~100 bare `(E##/F#/D#/X##)` citations whose only resolution is array-index positions inside a dated report; nothing in the body legends the convention or the path, so the plan is not self-contained for the executing seat and binds a report's volatile internal ordering rather than a stable identity.
expertFindings.evidence: `dispositions.v2.md` preamble: "One row per finding in `findings.v1.json` (80 expert E0–E79 **by array index**, 8 frame F0–F7, 10 landscape D0–D9, 31 dropped-at-cap X0–X30)". The plan body cites ids from W0.1 ("E46/E60") through W6.4 ("X10") with no legend; the only path mentions are the v1→v2 note and §Review record. ADR-127 §5 decoupling: references should depend on a document's stable identity, not volatile positional detail. The strategic node carries the same pattern ("v1-review finding E65") with no path at all.
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Add one legend line under the v1→v2 note ("E/F/D/X ids index `.agent/reports/design/plan-review-2026-08-02/findings.v1.json` per the array-index convention stated in `dispositions.v2.md`"), give the strategic node's citation the same path, and keep every story's substantive statement self-contained so the id reads as provenance rather than as content the reader must fetch.

expertFindings.section: §Out of scope / W6.3 — ADR-217 routing wording
expertFindings.claim: The plan twice routes "the MCP-app island-hydration/ADR-217 amendment tail" to MCP-448, but that amendment is already in the corpus; only the delivery tail remains, and an executor will look for an unlanded ADR edit.
expertFindings.evidence: `217-server-rendered-html-in-the-mcp-app.md` §1 carries "**Dated amendment (2026-07-31, recording the owner ruling of 2026-07-26)** … The delivery tail carrying that conversion (hydration client, theme control, renderer switch — recorded as deliberate deviations in PR #583's description) is owned by MCP-448; until it lands, the code deliberately bakes static markup at build time per PR #583." The v1 finding E58 made exactly this correction ("The 'ADR-217 amendment' named as transferring value is already on main"), and `dispositions.v2.md` records E58 as `applied`.
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Restate both occurrences as "the MCP-app hydration/theme-control DELIVERY tail that ADR-217 §1's 2026-07-31 amendment assigns to MCP-448", so W6.3's closure comment routes an existing obligation rather than an already-landed ADR edit.

expertFindings.section: W2 preamble, W2.1, W2.2, W2.6(c); §Relationships ADR obligations
expertFindings.claim: Identity data has no declared home in the package topology, so the thinness boundary rule W2.6(c) mandates cannot be written, and any home under packages/design/ is validator-red on landing with no amendment obligation recorded.
expertFindings.evidence: W2 names `design-tokens-core` as owning workspace for "schema + validators + emitter" but never says where identity manifests, the identity DTCG token files, the "declared identity CSS layer", or the emitted brand CSS live. W2.6(c) requires depcruise/eslint rules "no framework module imports identity data; no identity data imports framework source" — a two-sided rule whose second path set is undefined. W2.6(a) presupposes "the framework's importable tree". Today identity lives INSIDE the framework package at <repo>/packages/design/oak-design-system/studio-source/whitelabel/{creature,freedonia}/. If the home is a new packages/design/* workspace, <repo>/packages/core/oak-eslint/scripts/validate-boundaries.ts lines 77-80 fails it immediately — `assertEqual('Design boundary inventory', [...DESIGN_PACKAGE_IMPORTS].sort(...), actualDesignPackageNames)` — and `createDesignBoundaryRules` (boundary.ts:406) is exhaustive via `assertNever(designName)`, so a new member without its branch fails the build loudly. §Relationships' ADR-obligation map lists ADR-041 rows only for W1.1/W5.1 (demos), none for W2.
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Add a W2.0 story that names the identity home explicitly (new `packages/design/*` workspace, or a directory inside an existing one). If a workspace: make the `DESIGN_PACKAGE_IMPORTS` entry, the new `createDesignBoundaryRules` branch (both specifier and path-zone forms), and a dated ADR-041 design-row amendment acceptance lines of that story, and add the ADR-041 row to §Relationships' obligation map.

expertFindings.claim: Two of the four named roster consumers are forbidden by the standing, enforced design-tier boundary rules from importing the workspace the plan puts the roster in, so "derive from it" is unexecutable as written and no amendment is obligated.
expertFindings.evidence: W2.3 requires the generated roster to be "consumed by the kit runtime, the React types, the gate expectations, and the demo label maps", with the five hand-maintained lists deriving from it "or build-checked against it". Verified in <repo>/packages/core/oak-eslint/src/rules/boundary.ts: lines 450-464 give `oak-design-react` the message "can depend on '@oaknational/oak-design-system' only (the ADR-213 §4 tier edge)" with `@oaknational/design-tokens-core` explicitly in its restricted set; lines 466-497 bar `oak-design-system` from every design sibling AND from core — "The kit is the neutral trunk (ADR-213 §4): it imports nothing from the monorepo at runtime." The kit's own list is a zero-import browser script (`packages/design/oak-design-system/src/oak-theme.ts:31`, exempted as an orphan entry point at .dependency-cruiser.mjs:45), and `packages/design/oak-design-react/src/oak-theme-store.ts:38` hardcodes `export type OakThemeName = 'light' | 'dark' | 'system' | 'high-contrast' | 'colour-safe'`. Only `oak-design-tokens` may see both sides (boundary.ts:423-435), and it is where `design-system-expectations.ts` already lives. §Relationships obligates no ADR-041/boundary amendment for W2.3.
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Restate W2.3's mechanism per consumer: emit-into-the-consumer codegen (the kit's script and the tier's type file are generated outputs, not importers) plus a build-check owned by `oak-design-tokens`, the sole permitted join point. If any consumer must genuinely import the roster, add a dated ADR-041 intra-design amendment plus the `createDesignBoundaryRules` edit as W2.3 acceptance lines.

expertFindings.section: W3 preamble, W3.0 mapping rule; §Decision log; dispositions E14/E66
expertFindings.claim: W3.0's mapping rule is a total re-wrap mandate over the class library, so the recorded verdict that ADR-213 §3's standing rejection needs no amendment does not survive the plan's own text.
expertFindings.evidence: W3.0 records the rule as "recipe class → component; modifier class → prop/variant union; layout primitive → composition component; utility → `className` passthrough only", applied so that "every W0.1 component class gets a recorded mapping decision" (W3 preamble: "The owner's 'full component set' is satisfied as full COVERAGE"). There is no decline branch. `packages/design/oak-design-system/components.css` carries 102 distinct top-level `.oak-*` selectors (counted first-hand). ADR-213 §3 Standing rules: "Re-wrapping the class library in a framework component layer remains rejected... This question is settled here and is not re-litigated per widget." The 2026-07-23 §3 amendment reaffirms it verbatim under "Stands unchanged": "the rejection of re-wrapping the _class library itself_ in a component layer therefore also stands" — and describes the tier as CURATED: "adoption from `studio-source/` is curation on owner substance, not a second-consumer event." A total mapping function over the class census is the opposite of curation. The dispositions ledger records E14 as `applied` with "no re-wrap mandate remains, so the §3 rejection stands unamended".
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Give the mapping rule an explicit default-decline branch — coverage means a recorded DECISION per class, and the default decision is "no component; kit class consumed directly", with a component minted only where a materialised need is named (the §3 "first materialised need" doctrine). If the seat still wants class-driven minting, carry a dated ADR-213 §3 amendment with grounds as a W3.0 acceptance line rather than asserting the rejection is untouched.

expertFindings.section: W1.1 and W5.1 new-workspace plumbing contract
expertFindings.claim: The same story mandates a `no-cross-demo` boundary rule and cross-demo reuse of the test harness; executing it as written either fires the new rule or lands a third copy of a harness the estate just de-duplicated.
expertFindings.evidence: W1.1 enumerates "depcruise `no-packages-to-demos`/`no-cross-demo` rules" and, in the same sentence list, "hermetic cross-origin interception reused from the showcase" (W5.1 repeats the contract). The interception is demo-local: <repo>/demos/oak-design-showcase/tests/apply-state.ts imports `SHOWCASE_ORIGIN` from `../tools/showcase-origin`, and the assertions (`openShowcase`, `assertOnlyKnownExternalOrigins`) are consumed by `tests/showcase-a11y.spec.ts`. Importing them from a sibling demo is exactly what `no-cross-demo` forbids; copying them reproduces the defect ADR-041's 2026-08-02 amendment just cured for the theme store ("The demos consume `oak-design-react` for the shared `useSyncExternalStore` theme-store adapter; the two prior in-demo copies are deleted at this landing", 041 line 191-193).
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Add a W0 story (beside W0.8) hoisting the shared demos test harness — origin gate, cross-origin interception, apply-state — to a home above the demos tier, and have W1.1/W5.1 consume that home rather than "reuse from the showcase". Land the `no-cross-demo` rule in the same PR as the hoist so the rule is red-proven against the pre-hoist shape.

expertFindings.section: W0.8 Literal instruments re-homed; W1.1/W5.1 plumbing contract
expertFindings.claim: Only the literal walker is re-homed; the kit-asset parity guard stays a hand-enumerated roster inside one demo, so it goes vacuously green over the two new demos, which also have no declared kit-copy delivery mechanism.
expertFindings.evidence: W0.8 re-homes "the authored-CSS literal walker and its non-vacuity leg" with "the demo roster derived from the workspace inventory". The sibling instrument is not mentioned: <repo>/demos/oak-design-showcase/tools/kit-asset-parity.ts exports a hand-enumerated `KIT_ASSET_COPIES` manifest that already traverses into a sibling demo (`{ source: 'oak-theme.js', copy: '../oak-curriculum-hub/public/oak-theme.js' }`), and root package.json line 43 invokes it as `pnpm --filter @oaknational/oak-design-showcase validate-kit-assets` inside `repo-validators:check`. W1.2 requires "static HTML + kit stylesheets + `oak-theme.js`", which in a demo workspace means served tracked copies (the showcase's `public/oak-theme.js` and `public/brands/*` precedent), yet neither W1.1 nor W5.1 names a kit-copy mechanism or new manifest rows.
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Extend W0.8 to re-home `validate-kit-assets`/`kit-asset-parity` alongside the literal walker, with the copy roster derived from the workspace inventory rather than hand-enumerated, and add "kit-asset delivery + parity rows" to the enumerated W1.1/W5.1 plumbing contract.

expertFindings.claim: The section claims to carry "the estate edges v1 lacked" but omits the live backlog plan that owns the demos-tier boundary work W1.1/W5.1 land, breaching the plan's own one-owner-per-workstream rule.
expertFindings.evidence: <repo>/demos/README.md lines 11-12 name `.agent/plans-backlog-2026-07/curriculum-hub-demo/current/productionisation-and-reuse.plan.md` as owner of the demos-tier productionisation roadmap. That plan's frontmatter reads `status: 🟢 DECISION-COMPLETE (owner-ratified 2026-07-01 ~21:30Z) — QUEUED` and carries `ws0-topology-demos-tier`: "execute the ratified first-class demos/ tier — gate parity + one-way boundary + renames", plus `ws1-token-consolidation`. W1.1/W5.1 land precisely that one-way boundary. §Relationships names only `design-system-integration` and `mcp-137-design-system-semantic-merge`, while E54/E69's disposition asserts "exactly one plan owns each workstream".
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Add a §Relationships bullet for `productionisation-and-reuse` with a dated re-homing amendment for `ws0-topology-demos-tier` naming this node as carrier, and a one-line statement on `ws1-token-consolidation` (owned there, or superseded by ADR-213 Stage B).

expertFindings.claim: W0.8 leaves the re-homed instruments' home as a fork — "design tier or root repo-validators" — and the design-tier arm establishes a design→demos knowledge edge ADR-041's matrix does not sanction.
expertFindings.evidence: W0.8: "move above the demos tier (design tier or root repo-validators)". ADR-041's design row (line 73) permits core only and forbids apps; `demos/` has no row in the dependency-direction matrix at all (the ADR's own note at lines 53-57 explains the eight rows and does not include demos). `design-tokens-core` is additionally barred from every design sibling (boundary.ts:411-421). A design-tier validator walking `demos/**` inverts the tier direction the plan's own W2.6(c) thinness rule depends on. `validate-boundaries` already lives at packages/core/oak-eslint/scripts/, the natural precedent.
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Name the home explicitly in W0.8 — root repo-validators (`packages/core/oak-eslint/scripts/` or `agent-tools/src/validators/`), matching where `validate-boundaries` already sits — and drop the design-tier option.

expertFindings.claim: The planned ADR-041 amendment addresses only the Decision-list enumeration, leaving the demos tier with no row in the dependency-direction matrix — so the new depcruise rules have no ADR to derive from and the outbound allowance stays unencoded.
expertFindings.evidence: ADR-041 lines 33-37 are a Decision-list bullet ("demonstration apps consuming workspace package surfaces only... no boundary rule enforces the inbound direction yet; enforcement lands at need"). The matrix at lines 67-76 has eight rows and no demos row. The live outbound reality, verified from package.json: the hub consumes core (`@oaknational/result`), sdks (`curriculum-sdk`, `oak-search-sdk`) and design (`oak-design-system`, `oak-design-react`); the showcase consumes core (`type-helpers`) and design. W1.1/W5.1 mint only the inbound (`no-packages-to-demos`) and lateral (`no-cross-demo`) rules.
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Make the W1.1/W5.1 ADR-041 amendment add the `demos` matrix row (outbound: core / foundation libs / adapter libs / sdks / design yes; apps, agent-tools, agent-graphs, other demos no) as well as the two enumeration entries, so the three depcruise rules derive from a recorded constraint.

expertFindings.claim: "The emitted CSS replaces the hand-authored sheet" crosses the ADR-213 §1 production/source boundary and orphans the showcase's served copies; neither disposition is stated, while W1.2 states the equivalent mechanism explicitly for pages.
expertFindings.evidence: The hand-authored identity sheets are at packages/design/oak-design-system/studio-source/whitelabel/{creature,freedonia}/, and .dependency-cruiser.mjs lines 233-237 exclude `studio-source/` as "DESIGN-SYSTEM STUDIO SOURCE MATERIAL only (ADR-213; owner ruling 2026-07-19: production code gets no analysis exceptions)". ADR-213 §3's adoption mechanism is a move-out: "each adopted component moves out of `studio-source/` and under the full quality gate in the same change (the §1 production/source boundary rule is the adoption mechanism)". Those sheets are simultaneously a production delivery source: `kit-asset-parity.ts` maps `studio-source/whitelabel/freedonia/brand-full.css` to a served copy, and `demos/oak-design-showcase/components/useIdentity.ts` loads `/brands/${identity}/brand.css` from `demos/oak-design-showcase/public/brands/{creature,freedonia}/`. W1.2 declares the §1 mechanism "not triggered" for pages; W2.2 is silent for sheets, and the served copies are never dispositioned.
expertFindings.suggested_cure: State per identity in W2.2 whether the §1 move-out fires or the studio-source copy stays, and make the served-copy path (`public/brands/*`) plus its parity rows part of that identity's migration-landing acceptance, so no identity is served by both the authored and the emitted sheet.

expertFindings.section: Frontmatter comment on depends_on; §Relationships; dispositions E54/E69
expertFindings.claim: The body-carried blocking dependency is a route around a check rather than a fix of the condition the check reports: a live delivery node's only blocking edge is prose the estate cannot verify.
expertFindings.evidence: Verified first-hand that the deviation's grounds are accurate — agent-tools/src/validators/plan-schema/validate-plan-corpus.ts lines 36-40 scan only `.agent/plans/` ("The conserved backlog (`.agent/plans-backlog-2026-07/`)... [is] outside by construction") and validate-plan-corpus-helpers.ts:161-164 requires each edge to "name a plan id in the corpus". But the target is a LIVE plan: `.agent/plans-backlog-2026-07/architecture-and-infrastructure/current/design-system-integration.plan.md:76` reads "**Status**: 🟢 EXECUTING", it is ADR-213 §3's named executor, and this node amends three of its workstreams in place. The plan calls the validator's refusal "correct" (frontmatter comment) — the validator is correct, and what it is reporting is that a live dependency target is not in the corpus.
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Cure the condition rather than the symptom: either promote `design-system-integration` into `.agent/plans/` under the D23 schema, or mint a small corpus delivery node carrying the three re-homed workstreams, and then declare `depends_on: [{plan: <id>, kind: blocking}]` in frontmatter so the edge is machine-checked.

expertFindings.section: W0.3 The Demos Charter as doctrine
expertFindings.claim: The acceptance line acts on a `demos/README.md` §Charter section that does not exist, and the same story separately edits §Projects in the same file.
expertFindings.evidence: <repo>/demos/README.md has exactly four headings: `# Demos`, `## Dependency boundary`, `## Projects`, `## Licences`. W0.3 says the amendment lands "with `demos/README.md` §Charter reduced to a pointer plus a row-per-demo table" and its acceptance reads "README reduced"; the kit-side correction set in the same story separately names "`demos/README.md` §Projects".
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Restate as "add a §Charter section carrying a pointer to the ADR-213 amendment plus a row-per-demo table", and fold the §Projects correction into the same edit so one story makes one coherent change to that file.

expertFindings.claim: The enumerated correction set omits the design tier's own index README, which is stale by two workspaces at the moment the plan makes one of them first-class.
expertFindings.evidence: <repo>/packages/design/README.md lists only `oak-design-system`, `design-tokens-core`, `oak-design-tokens`, and `oak-design-ink` — omitting `oak-design-react` and `oak-design-assets`, both of which are live workspaces named in ADR-041's 2026-08-02 amendment and in `DESIGN_PACKAGE_IMPORTS` (boundary.ts:51-58). W0.3's correction set names `docs/consuming-nextjs.md`, the showcase README + package.json description, `demos/README.md` §Projects, and the ADR-041 demos row.
expertFindings.suggested_cure: Add `packages/design/README.md` to W0.3's enumerated correction set, with the two missing workspaces described by their tier role (React binding tier; shared design assets).

frameFindings.claim: The wow-first cure (F2) is applied only to the cheapest demo; the showcase — the object the owner actually rejected and the plan's centre of gravity — renders its first new pixel only after the entire W2 identity machinery (10 stories) and the W3 React tier, re-instating plumbing-before-pixels exactly where the bar binds hardest.
frameFindings.evidence: "Sequencing: W0 → W1 → W2 → W3 → W4 → W5 → W6" with W4 = "The showcase, rebuilt to the wow bar". The plan's own text carries the ruling it violates: "wow-first decomposition — early rendered pages with machinery underneath, never workstreams of plumbing before pixels". No technical dependency forces the wait: the W1 preamble proves pages need no React tier ("the plain demo consumes the kit directly — oak-theme.js is framework-neutral"), and the Decision log makes tier components "paint via kit classes", so a kit-class showcase page is visually identical to its post-W3 form. The biggest wow unknown — whether the W4.1 design grammar hits the bar — is discovered at maximum sunk cost.
frameFindings.suggested_cure: Pull W4.1 (design grammar + composed page set — it has no stated W2/W3 dependency) into W0/W1 time and add an early showcase wow probe: one or two composed showcase pages authored against kit classes, shown at an owner checkpoint before W2/W3 spend, with W3 component families landing beneath already-approved pixels page by page.

frameFindings.claim: The styled-components demo has no design or page-authoring story at all — W5.1 is plumbing, W5.2 is tier consumption, W5.3 is a lint rule, and W5.4 is "Wow checkpoint (owner-held)" with no named render object — so every repo-safe gate can pass while the demo is a thin token-discipline tech proof with nothing to wow at.
frameFindings.evidence: W5's complete story list: workspace contract, "Consumption through the tier", "Token discipline", "Wow checkpoint". Contrast W1.2, which names the plain demo's content ("The export's three composed pages, authored fresh against the live kit"). Nothing anywhere in W5 says what pages the demo contains, in what grammar, at what scope. Combined with the seat verdict that the styled demo consumes oak-design-react, the demo's natural minimal form is a page of re-wrapped tier components — precisely a mediocre outcome the owner's "each and every demo" bar rejects.
frameFindings.suggested_cure: Add a W5 content story symmetric with W1.2 — named composed pages in the export's grammar, same charter DoD, same W0.7 instrument pass — and define W5.4's checkpoint object as those pages.

frameFindings.claim: The specimen-grid ban removes v1's failure mode by name but not its generator: the W4.5 matrix still demands every census row land on a demonstrating surface, which pressures feature-dumping into the small composed page set — the complementary mediocrity (a lesson page carrying every badge, tag, and alert variant to satisfy matrix rows) passes the "primary content" clause and every mechanical gate while failing the bar.
frameFindings.evidence: W4.1: "census features are then mapped ONTO them"; W4.5: gate fails when "a census entry has no demonstrating surface", with "100% or owner-accepted" gaps each needing the owner's recorded word (high-friction, so inclusion is the path of least resistance). The reference tier is a "bounded exception". No density, features-per-page, or composition-budget constraint exists anywhere in the plan — demonstration density, the variable that actually decides whether a composed page reads as designed or as a dumping ground, is nobody's design decision.
frameFindings.suggested_cure: Make demonstration density a designed quantity: W4.1 names the page set WITH a per-page feature budget adjudicated by the W0.7 instrument; fold-into-composition dispositions are design decisions reviewed by the instrument, not mechanical census assignments; and low-glamour census rows can satisfy the matrix in the reference tier without per-gap owner ceremony.

frameFindings.claim: The design-review instrument — v2's cure for v1's one-line aesthetic instrument — is calibrated against one positive corpus and a single must-fail page, run once: an instrument that fails only the rejected page and passes everything else clears calibration while having zero measured power to discriminate mediocre from amazing, which is exactly the "process green, demos mediocre" failure this axis names.
frameFindings.evidence: W0.7: "the rejected showcase page = must-fail — red-then-green calibration, run once at landing". One negative example cannot bound the space between "not that page" and "amazing"; and "run once" means months of W4 landings ride an instrument whose miss rate against the owner's actual verdicts is never measured, even though §Quality bar 2 makes it the always-on gate before every render reaches him.
frameFindings.suggested_cure: Calibrate against a graded corpus — deliberately degraded variants of export pages (spacing, hierarchy, colour-discipline mutations) as additional must-fails — re-run calibration at each workstream open, and record the instrument's miss rate against owner wow verdicts so its blocking authority is earned, not assumed.

frameFindings.claim: Identity design authorship — the F5 cure — has owner-held "rendered identity checkpoints" but no identity-capable rendered surface exists at W2 time: identity switching is showcase-only and the showcase rebuild is W4, so the checkpoints either break the stated W2→W4 sequencing or render on W2.5's specimen-carrier pages — the bare-specimen genre the plan's own taste calibration records the owner as having REJECTED.
frameFindings.evidence: W2.9 acceptance: "(owner-held: rendered identity checkpoints...)" with no carrier named. §Out-of-scope: "identity switching in the plain and styled demos (recorded assumption, showcase-only...)". W2's only rendered surfaces are the W2.5 specimen-carrier page and the W2.6 synthetic fixture. §Direction taste calibration: "REJECTED — bare specimen grids". The one workstream whose whole point is proving the counter-identities are worth configuring would be judged on a surface genre the owner has already dismissed.
frameFindings.suggested_cure: Name the carrier: per-identity static builds of W1.2's composed pages (static builds need no switching, so the out-of-scope line is untouched) or an early showcase page, and bar specimen-carrier pages from ever being owner-checkpoint objects.

frameFindings.claim: The charter's composition rule plus W4.2's focus-order check jointly define the owner's standing requirement "CSS able to re-order page elements non-trivially" out of existence: any CSS-driven reorder makes DOM and visual order diverge, which the charter deems a defect to re-author, so the capability can only ever be demonstrated by re-authoring DOM order — which is not CSS re-ordering.
frameFindings.evidence: W0.3: "a variant whose DOM order and visual order diverge is a defect to re-author, not a feature". W4.2: every composition variant must "assert sequential focus order matches visual order (getBoundingClientRect monotonicity)". Yet W2.6's falsifier goes red "the moment an axis is unreachable from config" and its census axes include "composition ordering", and the standing owner requirement names non-trivial CSS re-ordering explicitly. The plan carries both sides of the contradiction without reconciling them; a detail lens reads each clause as individually sound.
frameFindings.suggested_cure: Replace the blanket defect rule with an explicit envelope — divergence permitted where reading order stays meaningful and focus order defensible per WCAG 1.3.2/2.4.3 (e.g. non-interactive, visual-rhythm reordering) — and name the surface that demonstrates non-trivial re-ordering so the owner requirement has a home instead of a prohibition.

frameFindings.claim: The hub is the plan's highest-risk wow surface — 548 recorded raw-value occurrences of accepted debt, built before the system matured — yet it is the only demo whose checkpoint sits at the very end (W6.2), with failure handled by an unshaped, unbudgeted contingency, so the plan can run to completion and then discover its largest visual cure with zero planned capacity.
frameFindings.evidence: W0.3 hub wow reading: "a failed checkpoint opens scoped visual-cure work (recorded assumption — the owner can overrule at the first hub checkpoint)" — no stories, no budget, no workstream. §Cross-demo: "548 arbitrary-value occurrences... RECORDED as accepted standing debt... reduced opportunistically". The bar is "each and every demo", and the hub exists TODAY — its wow verdict costs nothing to obtain now, but the plan defers it to last.
frameFindings.suggested_cure: Put the existing hub in front of the owner at W0 as a zero-cost wow pre-read; if it fails, mint scoped visual-cure stories into the plan body with a budget now, instead of a contingent clause discovered at the plan's end.

frameFindings.claim: The bar is per-DEMO ("look at each and every demo and think 'wow'") but every checkpoint is per-page: nothing judges demo-level cohesion — navigation, cross-page rhythm, coherence of the whole browsing experience — so four sets of individually-passed pages can assemble into demos that do not wow, and the long drip of per-page micro-verdicts risks degrading the owner's wow signal into checkpoint fatigue.
frameFindings.evidence: §Quality bar 1: "verdict recorded per page"; W1.3, W4.2, W4.3, W4.4 checkpoints are all page- or landing-scoped; W5.4 has no defined object; the only whole-surface moment is W6.2, and only for the hub. The W0.7 rubric's axes (type scale, spatial rhythm, hierarchy, colour discipline, composition grammar) are likewise all intra-page.
frameFindings.suggested_cure: Add a closing whole-demo checkpoint per demo — the owner browses the demo end-to-end in Chrome as its final owner-held acceptance — add a cross-page cohesion clause to the W0.7 rubric, and batch page verdicts so the owner experiences composed sets rather than a stream of single-page asks.

frameFindings.claim: Even the first-light cure sits behind a heavy corridor — fleet re-review to a zero-finding round, a tested census generator, full gate stabilisation INCLUDING a brand-new prefers-contrast feature, the instrument build, instrument re-homing, the charter ADR ceremony (W1.2's pre-paint and DoD cite it), and W1.1's full plumbing contract — so the first pixel the owner sees is still weeks of machinery away, against both the wow-first ruling and his wall-clock pricing.
frameFindings.evidence: W1 preamble gates first light on "W0's census/stabilise/instrument stories"; W0.2(c) is new product behaviour dressed as stabilisation ("a @media (prefers-contrast: more) CSS mapping... and the runtime consulting auto()" plus two new Playwright cells); §Quality bar 2 requires the instrument to run "BEFORE any render is shown", making W0.7's engineering a hard dependency of the first render; §Review record adds "iteration continues to a zero-finding round before implementation" ahead of all of it.
frameFindings.suggested_cure: Thin the critical path to first light: instrument v0 as rubric plus manual side-by-side (no generator engineering) with the mechanised form landing later; move W0.2(c) into W2's overlay work where it belongs conceptually; and let the first plain-demo render double as a live calibration sitting with the owner.

frameFindings.claim: The owner's "full optional React component set" is quietly reinterpreted as "full COVERAGE: every census class gets a recorded mapping decision" — a mapping decision (e.g. "utility → className passthrough only") is not a component, and the reading lives only as a plan clause, never surfaced to the owner as the decision it is.
frameFindings.evidence: W3 preamble: "The owner's 'full component set' is satisfied as full COVERAGE: every W0.1 component class gets a recorded mapping decision." Unlike the four flagged seat-verdicts, this reinterpretation is not in the Decision log and carries no owner-review moment.
frameFindings.suggested_cure: Card the reading to the owner at W3.0 (per surface-user-decisions-as-questions): components for recipe classes, props for modifiers, passthrough for utilities — confirm this satisfies "full set" — and record his answer in the Decision log.
